column4: Ta, akankāram conception of individuality, arrogance, haughtiness; änkāram id., kindness, love; ānkāri (-pp-, -tt-) to be arrogant, insolent. Ma. ahankāram, ānkāram feeling of self, pride, self-conceit, boisterousness. Ko. a'ŋkarm (obl. a.şka'rt-) joyful pride, joyfulness. Ka. ahamkāra concept of individuality, pride; ahamkarisu to be proud. Tu. ahankāra, ānkāra self-consciousness, pride, haughtiness; ahankaripuni, ankariyuni to be proud, arrogant. Te. ahankāramu, (K also) ãkaramu egotism, pride, arrogance; ahankarincu to be arrogant. Skt. ahamkāra- conception of one's individuality, pride, haughtiness.

Ta. akattiyam, akattiyam-āy without fail, surely, certainly. Ka. agatya indispensableness, necessity, want; agatyav-āgi necessarily, urgently, positively, by all means. Tu. agatya need, necessity, want; urgent, important. Te. agatyamu necessity, need; urgent, necessary, needful, important; agatyamu-gā urgently, necessarily, positively, certainly. Skt. agati want of resource, necessity, distress (so Kitt.); difficult from the point of view of meaning, whereas Skt. avaśyam, which corresponds exactly in meaning, presents phonetic difficulties (but not perhaps altogether insuperable).

Ta. akkiramam irregularity, injustice. Ma. akramam disorder, irregularity, crime. Ko. akrm (obl. akrt-) evil actions (? rather < Skt. akarman improper action, crime; cf. Ka. akarma id.). To. okira'm treachery. Ka. akrama confusion, injustice. Tu. akrama irregularity, confusion. Te, akramamu irregularity, misconduct, injustice, impropriety. /Skt. akrama want of order, confusion; (Bilhana, Vikramankadevacarita 14.11, 22) improper course of conduct.

Ta. akkam price of grain. Ko. agm rate at which measures of grain are sold for the rupee. Ka. agga, hagga price, cheapness, cheap. Tu. agga cheapness; aggalāsy, aggysy cheap. Te. agguva cheapness; (K) agguvu price. /Skt. argha- value, price. Pa. Pkt. aggha- id.

Ta. akki fire, heat. Ma. akki fire. To, ox- (oxy-) to burn to ashes (intr.; wood, house, corpse). Ka. ag(g)i, haggi fire. Kod. agg- (aggi-) (fire) consumes everything and becomes bed of coals. Tu, aggi fire. Te, aggi id. /Skt. agni fire. Pa. Pkt. aggi- id. Perhaps the verbs are not derived from IA, but by assimilation from *arg-; cf. DED 234. 10 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN accu accu

Ta. acațțai contempt, disdain, inattention, indifference; acattālam filthiness, disorder, muddle. Ma. aśraddha neglect. Ka. asadde dislike, disdain, scorn; asadļāla contemptibleness, unlawful action, ugliness. Tu. asadde disdain, contempt, negligence. Te. asadda neglect, inattention, (B also) disdain, contempt; aśraddha neglect, inattention, carelessness. /Skt. aśraddha want of trust, unbelief. Pkt. asaddhā- id.

Ta. accu axle, axle-bolt. Ma. accu, accittați axle-tree. Ka. axle. Tu. accida mara axle-tree; add-acci axle. Te. (K, dial.) id. Kol. (SR) äskud id. Nk. āk, āckurid. Pa. ackurid. /Skt. akşa- axle. Pa. Pkt. akkha id. Mar. ās id. Bihari (Grierson, Bihar Peasant Life, p. 32) ak main beam in the rear of the cart. Turner, s. v. akhārā.

Ta. aticayam excellence, pre-eminence; astonishment, wonder; aticayi (-pp-, -tt-) to wonder, be surprised. Ma. atiśayam pre-eminence, uncommon; marvel, wonder; atiśayikka to excel; to wonder, be surprised. Ko. adycm (obl. adyct-) wonder, a wonder. Ka. atiśaya pre-eminence; wonder, surprise; pre-eminent; wonderful; atiśayam-badu to wonder, be surprised; atiśayisu to become, or make, great; to wonder. Koờ. adi a wonder. Tu. atiśaya pre-eminence; wonder, marvel. Te. atiśayamu pre-eminence; marvellous, excessive, wonderful; atiśayincu, atiśayillu to increase, surpass. Skt. atisaya- pre-eminence; pre-eminent. L. V.R. 1934.253-4.

Ta. atiţtam that which is unseen; merit or sin accruing from actions; luck, fortune; atirustam that which is not seen; luck, good luck. Ma. adſştam fortune, luck; (coll.) atiștam ill-luck, influence of the evil eye. Ko. adişțm (obl. adiștt-) good fortune. Ka. adrsta destiny; luck, good luck. Tu. adrșța fortune, fate. Te. adrșțamu fortune, luck; adſșțavantūņu, adṛṣṭaśāli a fortunate man. /Skt. adşșța- invisible; destiny (good or bad). Pkt. ad(d)iţtha id. L. V.R. 1934.255,
Ta. atti long pepper. Ma. atti elephant pepper. /? < Skt. hasti-pippali Scindapsus officinalis. Pkt. hatthi-pippali id.

Ta. attuvānam ruins, desert, desolate place. Ma. addhvānam great exertion, fatigue; addhvāni diligent; addhvānikka to labor, work hard, exert oneself. Ka. adhvāna wilderness, forest, desert; misfortune; dearness, excess of price; (coll., L. V.R. 1934.255) immethodical, weak, bad, spoiled, useless. Tu. adhvana, advåna labor, immethodical effort; tired, weak, wrong, spoiled; addana weakness, sickness, affliction. Te. adhvānamu desolation, waste, ruin; adhvānapu desolate, waste, spoiled, bad, (B also) perplexing; adhvānamu cēyu to ruin, lay waste, spoil. /Skt. adhvan- (acc. adhvānam) road, journey, distance. L. V.R. 1934. 255-256. DICTIONARY 11 even-

Ta. antastu rank, condition; story of a building. Ka. antastu being between; being one above another, tier, story of a building; degree of dignity, rank. Tu. antasty upper story or room; a secret. Te. antastu story of a house; arrangement of one above another; dignity, prestige. Skt. antaḥstha- being in the midst or between. L. V.R. 1934.257.

Ta. anti twilight, morning and evening prayers. Ma. anti ing. Ko. ande:l time after sunset until about 9 P. M.; ande:l poſt afternoon from about 4 to 6 P. M.; inde:l this last night, yesterday night; this coming evening. Koạ. andi evening just after dark; andi-kotti evening star in west. Skt. samdhi- interval between day and night, twilight.
Ta. appatſam unmixed, pure. Ka. appața id. Te. appațamu id., unadulterated. Skt. asprsta- untouched. But the MIA forms of Skt. sprś- have u in general.

Ta. appaņai command. Ka. appane order, command, law; permission, leave. Kod. appaņe order. Tu. appaņè command, order; permission, leave. Te. appaņa, appana id. Skt. ājñāpana- ordering (so Ta. Lex., Kitt.). ? Skt. arpaņa- consigning, entrusting; Pkt. appaņaid.
Ta. amayam, amaiyam opportunity, occasion. fit or convenient time, opportunity, festive occasion, season. /Skt. samayaopportunity, occasion, season.

Ma. amparam, amparam hog-plum, wild mango, Spondias mangifera. Ka. amațe, ambațe, ambața, ambāde, avaje id. Tu. ambațe, ambaờè id. Skt. ambarișa-, amlavāțaka-, ämravățaka-, āmrātaka- id. Pa. ambāțaka id. Pkt. ambāda(g)a- id. H. ābārā, Mar. ābādā id. Turner, S. V. amaro.
Ta. arankam island formed by a river or rivers, delta. Te. lanka island, islet. (Cf. Skt. lankā-.

Ta. aran, aranam defence, fortress; araņi (-pp-, -tt-) to fortify, defend; araņiya adj. defended; araṇ-manai royal palace, mansion. Ma. aran stronghold; araṇippu being impregnable. /Skt. śaraṇa- shelter. Skt. arana- refuge < Dr.

Ta. aruttam, arttam meaning, intention, wealth, usefulness, etc. Ma. artham aim, wealth, meaning. Ko. artm (obl. art(t)-) meaning, a sententia, proverbial saying. To. artm (obl. art-) meaning, useful- Ka. artha aim, utility, meaning, wealth, etc. Tu. artha wealth, meaning. Te. arthamu meaning, object, wealth, use, etc. /Skt. arthaaim, use, object, wealth, meaning, etc. Ka. amaga 18 ness. 12 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 22
Ta. arukkam crystal. To. ark glass (window or a piece of glass). Ka. arka crystal. Tu. arka id. Te. arkamu id. /Skt. arka- crystal.
Ta. allam, nallam ginger; ? ellam id. Ka. alla green ginger. Te. allamu id. Kuwi (S) alomi ginger. Skt. ārdra(ka)- fresh ginger. Pkt. alla-, allaa- id. Mar. ălē id. Turner, s.v. aduwa.

Ma. avakațam, apakațam mischief, danger. Ka. avagada, avagadike obstruction, jeopardy, monstrosity. Tu. avagada calamity, mischief, danger; disorder, confusion. Te. avakațamu Te. avakatamu opposition; avagadamu mischief, mischievous deed, carelessness, danger; bad, undesirable. Skt. avakața- opposite, contrary (so apparently in the lexica; taught in Pāṇini 5.2.30, but without meaning); L. V.R. 1934. 257. Mar. avaghad difficult, difficulty, calamity; avaghadņē to be in straits. Godavarma, p. 14: Skt. apakşta- injury, offence > Pkt. *apakața-. Cf. also 28 Ta. akațiyam.

Ta. avacaram favorable opportunity; hurry, urgency, necessity, compulsion. Ko. avca.rm (obl. avca'rt-) hurry, urgency. To. ofso'rm id. Ka. avasara necessity, urgency, hurry; avasarisu to make haste, be eager. Tu. avasara, avasāra, amasara necessity, urgency, hurry. Te. avasaramu occasion; necessity, need, urgency, haste, hurry; necessary, urgent; avasara-padu to hurry, hasten. Skt. avasara favorable opportunity, seasonableness. L. V. R. 1934, 258.

Ta. avati limit; suffering, distress. Ma. avadhi-ppețuka to be pressed Ka. avadhi limit; extremity, calamity, misfortune. Te, avadhi (B.; coll.) calamity, misfortune; (K) avadhĩ-bettu to put to trouble; avadhĩ -bovu to be troubled, perish, go to waste. /Skt. avadhi- term, limit. L. V.R. 1934, 257-8.

Ta. avantarai disorder, confusion, forlornness, becoming useless, fruitless. Ka, abandara, abandare disorder, irregularity, uselessness, waste. Te. abandara disorder, confusion, irregularity. /Skt. abandhuram dejectedly, sadly (śiśupālavadha 6.29; comm., - aśobhana-).
Ta. aniram, anutam, anuşam the 17th nakṣatra (i.e. lupus and scorpion's head). Ma. anuram id. Skt. anurādhā- id. Ā

Ta. akațiyam mockery, ridicule, mischief, cruelty. Ka, āgada sport, jesting, mockery, insult, wantonness; āgadakāra scoffer; ägaļigatana insulting behavior. Te, āgadamu mischief, wantonness, prankishness; āgadakõdu, āgaļīdu scoffer, mischievous man. [Cf. 23 Ma. avakatam, DICTIONARY 13 com-

Ta. ākāttiyam pretence simulating agony or injury, outrageous behavior such as threatening to commit suicide. Ka. agātya id. Te. āgātyamu, āgāyityamu outrageous behavior, obstinacy, a desperate act, pretence of agony or injury, impropriety. Prob. Skt. āghātay-; cf. esp. BHS āghāta- malicious feeling, anger, hatred.

Ta. ācāri title adopted by Madhva and śri Vaişņava Brāhmans; title of the five artisan castes; ācān teacher, elder, priest; ācāļ priest's wife, lady of position; āciriyan priest, teacher, author of any literary work, scholar. Ma. ācāryyan fencing-master, schoolmaster, carpenter; ācăn, āśān schoolmaster; ācāri, aśări carpenter, sculptor of idols. Ka. ācāri title assumed by brahmin cooks, idol-makers, smiths, carpenters, goldsmiths, artificers. Kod. ayri (? a'yri) man of carpenter caste, blacksmith. Tu. acari a smith or carpenter. Te. acāri (= Ka.). /Skt. ācārya a spiritual guide or teacher. L. V.R. 1934. 259.
Ta. āți the fourth Tamil month, July-August; the 21st nakṣatra. Ma. āți id. Tu. āți id. Skt. äşāṇhā- the 21st and 22nd nakșatras.

Ta. āņai command; oath (as in a court of justice), profane swearing, vow; āņaiy-iţu to issue an order, take an oath, swear. Ma. āņa command, oath, adjuration; āņay-ițuka to swear, adjure. Ka. āne mand; oath, adjuration; āņe idu to swear. Kod. a ne a curse; a'ạe idto curse. Tu. āne oath; āja oath, curse, swearing; āja korpuni to swear; āja pāņuni to curse. Te. ana order, command; oath, adjuration; ană-bettu to adjure. /Skt. ājñā- order, command; (L. V. R. 1934. 260). Pkt. āņaid. H. an id. Mar. āņ oath, vow. Turner, s. v. jännu (Add.).

Ta. ātēcam rule, command, precept. Ma. ādēsam order, command. Ko. a'de:cm (obl. a.de.ct-) allotted or fated span of life. To. o Dişțm (obl. o Biștt-) fore-ordained length of life, long life. Ka. ādēša precept, order, command; adişța commanded. Te. adēšamu order, precept. Skt. adeśa- instruction, rule, order, foretelling; ādişța- directed, ordered.

Ta. åttiram impatience, eager haste, hastiness of temper; ättirakkāran over-anxious person, one who is impatient; aturam impatience, undue haste. Ma. āttaram necessity of engaging in a work. Ka. ãtura diseased, agitated by morbid desire; agitation, excitement, haste, hurry; longing for, great desire; aturagāra man who acts hastily or inconsiderately; āturisu to feel desire, etc. Tu. atura eagerness, haste. Te. at(u)ramu haste, impatience; atura-paļu to hurry; aturapāțu haste; atragădu a hasty man; (K; modern) adurdā haste, anxiety (< Skt. ãturată-). [Skt. åtura- suffering, sick, desirous. 14 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO- ARYAN

Ta. āpācam fallacy, reflection; that which is filthy; apātan impure person, wicked man. Ma. ābhāsam low, vulgar. Ka. ābāsa, ābāsu fallacy, incorrectness (as of speech), failure, defect, insufficiency (as of a meal); abāsa incongruity; abāsu disagreeableness of smell. Tu. abhāsa worthless, vulgar, corrupt. Te. abhāsamu, abhāsu disagreeable, bad, worthless; embarrassment. / Skt. abhāsa splendor, color, appearance, phantom, fallacious appearance, fallacy. L. V.R. 1934. 261.
Ko. a'rabm work of cultivation. Ka. aramba, ārambu tillage, cultivation. Te. ārabamu vegetation, crops, (B also) cultivation, tillage. Prob. Skt. arambha- undertaking, beginning.

Ka. ārõgisu to eat; ārögana, ārögane eating, a meal. Tu. ārögane meal, repast. Te, āragincu to eat, drink; āraginta, āragimpu, ārögiņamu eating. /Pkt. aroggia- 'bhukta-' (DNM). Mar. arogan making a meal, eating.

Ta. ārccanam earning, acquisition; ārcci (-pp-, -tt-) to earn, acquire. Ma. arjanam acquiring. Ka. arjana, ārjane procuring, gaining; ărjisu to acquire, earn. Tu. ārjita acquired, inherited. Te. ārjana income, remunerative job; ārjincu to earn, acquire, gain. Kui arji income, return for expenditure; arji āva to earn, receive an income. Kur. arja'ānā to earn, gain (as a profit or advantage), acquire. Skt. arjto acquire, gain, earn. BHS ārjanā- winning, acquisition; ārjay- to win. . H. arjnā to acquire, earn; v.n. arjan. Turner, s. v. arjan and arjan.
Ta. avaại the 5th Tamil month, August-September; the 22nd nakṣatra. Ma. avaņi id. Ka. āvaņi id. Skt. śrāvaņa- id. Cf. 62 Ta. õņam.

Ta. asti property, wealth. Ma. asti id.; ästikäran wealthy. Ka. ăsti property, wealth; ăstika, āstigāra man of property. Kod. a'sti property. Tu. āsti property, wealth. Te. asti id.; astikādu wealthy man. /Skt. astimat- possessed of property, opulent. BHS asti (? ăsti), abstracted from sarvāsti 'all property.' 40 I

Ta. ițți, īțți spear, lance. Ma. itti stick, spear; iſti staff of spear, pike. Ko. ic sword, spear, sharp point. To. ițy, i'ty spear. Ka. içți, iți lance, spear, javelin. Kod. îțți ferrule of stick; i:ți, (Mercara) ï'ți spear. Tu. īți id. Te. ite, ſtiya id. Konda īța id. Kuwi (S) ite id. Skt. ſștí- spear, lance. Pa. ițțhi- id. (Jätaka vi.223, which Pali Text Society Dict. erroneously tries to correct). DICTIONARY 15

Ta. ițţikai brick. Ma. ițţika id. Ko. it gal id. To. ițy, ity xal id. (in poetry). Ka. ițțige, ițțage, ițțangi, īțangi id. Tu. ittige id. Te. it(t)ika id. Kuwi (S) itteke illu tiled house. /Skt. iştakā-, işţikābrick. Pa. ițțhakā- id. Pkt. itthagā- id. U 43 ance.

Ta. ukkirāņam storehouse for provisions, granary; ukkirāņi storekeeper, steward. Ma. ugrānam (g, not k) storehouse, granary. Ka. ugrāņa id., treasury; ugrāņi storekeeper. Tu. ugrāņa, ugrāṇige storeroom; ugrāņi storekeeper, steward. Te. ugrāṇamu storehouse, storeroom. /Mar. ugrāņi gathering in of moneys due, sum aggregate of moneys collected.

Ta. uti (-pp-, -tt-) to swell, increase in size; rise, appear (as a heavenly body), come into existence, be born; utippu birth, appear- Ma. udikka (d, not t) to rise; udyal (d, not t) the rising sun. Ko. ut- (uty-) (sun, moon) rises; utn the east. To. wït- (wïty-) to increase (rain, wind), rise in pride; ut- (uty-) to increase (song-word; borrowed). Ka. uday(i)su, udisu to rise, be born. Kod. udi- (udip-, udic-) (sun) rises. Tu. udiyuni, udipini to rise (as the sun), be generated; udipāvuni to beget; udi, udaya rising of the sun, moon, or other heavenly bodies; udupu act of coming into existence. Te. udayamu rising of the sun, etc.; udayincu to rise, be born. /Skt. ud-i to rise; vin. udaya-.

Ta. uttaravu answer, reply; order, command, grant, leave; uttaram answer, reply. Ma. uttaravu command, leave; uttaram answer; command, letter. Ko. utarv permission, order. To, uturm (obl. uturt-) permission, order. Ka. uttara answer, reply; a mandate. Te. uttaruvu order, command, permission, leave; uttaramu answer, reply; letter, epistle. / Skt. uttara answer, reply. L. V.R. 1934, 261.
Ta. utakam water; utakännam food and drink. Ma. udakam (d, not t) water. Ko. udk broth (esp. made from meat). Ka. udaka water. Tu. udaka id. Te. udakamu id. /Skt. udaka water.

Ta. uttiyokam effort, exertion; business, employment. Ma. udyõgam exertion, industry; office, employment. Ko. udye v government appointment; udye.ga'rn government official. To. udy government appointment. Ka, udyoga exertion; business, an occupation, an office. Tu, udyoga exertion; business, occupation, employment. Te. udyogamu exertion; work, employment, occupation, office. /Skt. udyoga- act of undertaking, exertion. 16 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 1 Ka. unne 51
Ma. unnam stuffing, the cotton of the silk-cotton tree. wool. Te. unni wool. /Pkt. uņņā-, unna wool (< Skt. úrņā- id.).

To. uby heat. Ka. ubbe heat, steam. Tu. ube steam. Te. ubba closeness of weather, sultriness, heat. Kol. uba, (Haig) ubbā heat of sun. Nk. ubba id. /Mar. ūb, ub heat (cf. H. übh; < *umbha- (cf. Pischel $267] < Pkt. umha- < Skt. ūşman-).
Ta. upparikai, uparikai upper story. Ka. upparige palace, upper story of a house. Tu. upparige upper story of a house. Te. uppariga, upparige id. Skt. upakārikā- palace; ? influenced by upari.

Ta. ūmattai, ūmattam, ūmattu thorn-apple, Datura. Ma. ummam, ummattu D. metel. Ko. umat D. stramonium. Ka. um(m)atta, ummata, ummat(t)i, ummutta, ummetti thorn-apple, D. metel and fastuosa. Tu. ummuta purple thorn-apple, D. fastuosa; umbuge, umbucce, umbè whiteflowered thorn-apple, D. alba. Te. ummet(t)a D. alba and fastuosa. /Skt. unmatta D. metel and fastuosa. Pkt. ummatta- id. (DNM). (D. fastuosa Linn.; var. alba (D. alba Nees = D. metel Roxb.). D. metel Linn.)

Ta. ulakam, ulaku the earth, world, country, mankind, usage, sky; ulakattār people of the world, great men; ulakar, ulakor people of the world; ulak-iyal custom; ulokam the world. Ma. ulakam, ulaku world, earth. Ko. olgm (obl. olgt-) the world. /Skt. uloká-, lokáworld.

Ta. uluppai presents or supplies given to great personage. To. wilpy things bought for ceremonies or festivals. Ka. uluphe, ulipe supplies furnished gratuitously to great persons on a journey by villagers. Te, ulupă id. / H. ‘ulūfa rations, subsistence allowance (< Ar.).

Ta. uvā, uvavu, vāvu full moon, new moon. Ma. uvā fullness; uvāvu full moon; vāvu change of moon (chiefly full moon), holiday. Ko. una v full moon (un full); ața'v 8th day after new moon or after full moon (aŭ eight). Kod. ba'vu day of new moon or full moon. /Skt. upavāsa- a fast. Pkt. ovāsa id. Ē То. e'ny

Ta. ēņi, cēņi tier, ladder. Ma, ēņi ladder, bamboo used as ladder. Ko. e'n! ladder. id. Ka. ēņi id. Kod. ë:ņi id. Tu. ēņi, eņci id. Skt. śreņi- line, row. Pkt. seņi- id. Cf. Skt. nilḥ)śrayaņi-, nilḥ)śreņi-, niḥśreņikā- ladder.

Ta. ēļitam, ēļanam mockery, jeer. Ma. ēļitam contempt, DICTIONARY 17 mockery. Ka. ēļida id., abuse, disgrace; a contemptible man; ēļisu to censure, reprove, contemn, throw into the shade, eclipse. Te. ēlidamu, ellidamu scorn, contempt, disregard, inferiority; ellidūdu a contemptible person, man of low rank (cf. DED 728). Skt. helana- disregard, contempt. Godavarma gives helita-, which seems not to be attested in the literature. The Skt. hel-, heç- may be borrowed from Dr.; cf. DED 676.

Ta ēsaņai desire. Ma. ēşanam seeking, wishing. Ko. e'can reflection within the mind, consultation between people. To. e'za'n giy to ponder. Ka. ēşaņe seeking, begging, desire; ēşaņa seeking, begging O n, mov-

Ta. oñcari to go sideways; close partially (as a door). Ka. õsarisu to go to one side, sideways, or aside, turn aside, retreat, yield, go away, keep aloof, hesitate, stop; put to one side, remove, abandon; osara going to one side, sloping; õsarike state of bending to one side, etc. Te. Ösarincu to put aside; osarinta, orasimpu ing aside; osarilu, ösaru, õrasilu to move aside (intr.). /Turner, s.v. osārnu, says: "Skt. apasărayati lets go, removes; or (more probably) avasarayati moves aside." But Pa. avasarati, osarati, and BHS avasarati, osarati, mean approaches, arrives, while Pkt. has osar leave, which must surely (with Pischel SS154, 477, and Sheth) be < apa-sſ (Pkt. acc. to Sheth also has osar arrive <ava-sp).

Ta. oțțan member of a caste of diggers; fem. oțțacci. Ma. oţtar, oțțiyar people of the tank-digger's caste. Ka. odda class of people who cut stones from the earth, dig tanks and wells, etc.; fem. oddati; adj. odại. Kod. oddë man of caste of snake-charmers; fem. oddati. Te. odde man of the tribe of tank-diggers; native of Orissa. /Skt. odra- Orissa; the inhabitants of Orissa; (acc. to Manu) a tribe of Śūdras. Pkt. odda Orissa; inhabitant of Orissa. Turner, s.v. or.

Ta, oyyāram gracefulness of movement, foppery. Ka. oyyāra, vayyāra going about for show, parade, coquetry, beauty, grace; oyyāri showy man or woman. Tu. oyyāra coquetry, foppery. Te. oy(y)āramu beauty, affectation, coquetry; oy(y)āri beautiful woman. /Skt. vihārawalking for pleasure or amusement, play, pastime, diversion (so Kitt.). 18 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN o

Ta. Öcan preceptor, teacher. Ka. õja teacher, guru; artificer, carpenter, blacksmith, goldsmith. Te. õja, ojja teacher, tutor, master; (B) õju id.; goldsmith. Skt. upādhāya- teacher. Turner, s.v. ojhā. Cf. DED 874.

Ta. õņam the fifth Tamil month, August-September; the 22nd nakṣatra. Ma. õņam the 22nd constellation, Aquila; the national feast on new moon of September. Kod. 0'ņa the Malabar festival corresponding to Coorg puttëri rice harvest festival, /Skt. śroņă-, śrāvaņa- n. pr. nakșatra. Cf. 39 Ta. avaņi.

Ta. õlakkam assembly of state, durbar, hall. Ma. õlakkam splendor, majesty. Ka. Olaga service, homage; assembly, durbar; õlagisu, olaysu, õlavisu to serve, pay homage to; assemble, bring together. Tu. õlaga, õlega band of musicians; royal assembly, durbar; õlayi menial service of Pariahs; Õlayipuni to serve, do homage; öleguni to sit in state. Te. õlagamu assembly, meeting, court held by a sovereign, hall of audience; õlagincu to serve. | Pkt. olagg- to follow (cf. Skt. avalagna- hanging down from), do service; olaggā- attendance, service.
Ta. Õļi a continuous line, row. Ka. oļi, öņi id., multitude, succession. Te. õli a row, line, order. Malt. oli lineage, descent. Skt. avali- row, line, series, lineage. Pkt. oli- id. K, G mus.

Ta. kakkari kakri-melon, Cucumis melo-utilissimus. Ma. kakkari, kakkiri C. sativus. Ka. karkați, kankadi id. Skt. karkați- C. utilissi- Pkt. kakkadi- id. H. kakşi id. Turner, s.v. kẫkri, kəkro. [C. melo Linn. C. utilissimus Roxb. C. sativus Linn. is another species.)

Ta. kaccoram, kaccolam, kiccili long zedoary, Curcuma zedoaria; spiked garland-flower, camphor zedoary, Hedychium coronarium. Ma. kaccoram, kaccõlam C. zerumbet or Kæmpferia galanga. Ka. kacu, kacūra, kacora, kacchure, kacchöra, karcūra, karcūraka long zedoary, C. zerumbet Roxb., and its root; kaccūra K. galanga Linn. Tu. kaccūra a fragrant root of Zedoary zerumbet or C. zerumbet; K. galanga. Te. kacõramu, kaccūrakamu C. zedoaria. / Skt. kacora- C. zerumbet; kacchură-, kacchora a kind of turmeric; karcūra(ka)- turmeric. H. kacur C. zerumbet. [C. zedoaria Rosc. = C. zerumbet Roxb.; C. longa, DICTIONARY 19 which is turmeric, is a different species. All the others are different species.)

Ta. kañcam bell-metal, drinking vessel; kañcakāran brazier. To. koc brass; kocxo'rn man who makes brass vessels, clever worker. Ka. kañcu, kañca white copper or brass, bell-metal; a vessel made of bell-metal, etc.; kañcagāra brazier, coppersmith. Tu. kañci, kañcu bell-metal; kañcigāre brazier. Te. kancu bell-metal, bronze; kancara bell-metal work. Kuwi (S) kanzu (? c) bell-metal. Skt. kamsabell-metal, brass, white copper; vessel made of metal.

Ta. kațțai firewood, piece of timber. Ko. kat log. To. katy id.; wooden leg. Ka. kațțige piece of wood or timber, stick, club; kadi small stick, bit of wood. Kod. kaļļi id. Tu. kațțige fuel, firewood. Te. kațțiya, kațțe stick, staff, rod, piece of wood. Go. kația a piece of wood; (W, Ph.) kațiya wood; (A) kațțe firewood. Skt. kāştha- piece of wood, stick. Pkt. kațțha- id. Turner, s. v. kāțh.

Ta. kanakku account, calculation, arithmetic, account book, manner, way; kanakkan accountant. Ma. kanakku account, computation, manner, way; kanakkan accountant. Ko. kank calculation, records (government), historical account. To. koņk calculation, arithmetic. /Skt. gañaka- arithmetician, astrologer.

Ta. kanțam critical period, calamitous effect of the malignity of planets ruling the destiny of a person according to his horoscope. Ma. gandāntam a perilous time (astrol.). Ka. ganda baneful influence of a star; force or fierceness of disease, rain, wind, etc. Tu. gandāntara danger, peril. Te. gandamu id. Skt. ganda-, gandānta- (astrological terms).

Ta. kanți (-pp-, -tt-) to reprove, chide, speak with decision, precision, impartiality; kaņțippu reproof, strictness, exactness, precision, certainty; kanțitam sternness. Ma. khaņņikka to decide, settle, thwart, refute; khandippu decision, strictness, accuracy. Ko. kandip certainty; kandipa'r with certainty, surely. with certainty, surely. To. koạip strictly, accurately. Ka. kaņạita, khanạita firmness, positiveness, strictness, certainty; kandisu to settle (esp. the price of a thing). Koď. kandita tainty, fixing of a price. Tu. khanạita strict, severe, positive, certain; strictly, positively; khandisuni to fix, settle. Te. khaṇdincu to refute, disprove, criticize; khaṇạitamu decided, certain, strict; khaṇdimpu settlement, decision. /Skt. khand- to break, cut, destroy, defeat, refute (the meaning developments start from the last meaning given).

Ta. kattari scissors, shears, rat-trap; (-pp-, -tt-) to cut with scissors, clip, shear, gnaw (as insects, vermin), chop off; kattarikai cer- 20 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN scissors, shears. Ma. kattiri, katrika id.; katrikka to shear, clip. Ko. kata'ry spring-trap for rats. Ka. kattari scissors, shears, knife; kattarisu to cut with scissors or scissor-like things as teeth, cut off, shear. Kod. katri scissors. Tu. kattari, katteri scissors, shears, rat trap; katteriyuni, katteruni to shear, cut with scissors. Te. kattera scissors, shears; kattirincu to shear, scissor, crop, clip; kattiril(1) to be cut. Kuwi (S) katheri scissors. /Skt. kartarĨ- scissors. Pkt. kattari- id. Cf. DED 1012, Ta. katti knife, etc.
Ka. gaddige, gadduge, garduge throne, seat of honor. Tu. gaddige id. Te. gaddiya, gadde id. H. gādi, gaddi id. Turner, s.v. gādi.

Ta. kapaļu, kavațu deceit; kapați, kapatan, kavați a cheat, deceiver, knave. Ma. kapaļu, kapațam deceit, trick, sham. Ko. kavş deceit; kavaş Kurumba man; fem. kavaſc. To. kafoțxo'rn clever man; kafïd cunning, trick. Ka. kapața, kabața, kavada fraud, deceit, hypocrisy; kapați, kavați, kapatagara a deceitful person. Tu. kapața, kabata fraud, deceit; kapați hypocrite; kabațe a dissembling woman. Te. kapatamu hypocrisy; kapați hypocrite. Pa. kapaț deceit. Skt. kapatafraud, deceit. Pkt. kavada- id.

Ta. kapilai waterlift consisting of a large hemispherical bucket worked with bullocks; kavalai a kind of waterlift; kappi pulley. Ma. kappi id. Ka. kapali, kapale, kapile, kavile, kavule apparatus for raising water, consisting of pulley, rope, and bucket, worked by oxen on an inclined plane. Tu. kapi pulley. Te. kapile contrivance for raising water from a well. /H. kapi pulley, block (? < Ar. qabb hole in pulley-block).

Ta. kampaļi, kampalam coarse woollen blanket. Ma. kampili woollen cloth, blanket. Ko. kabey?, kabeylg, kabi'lg blanket. Ka. kambala, kambali id. Kod. kambīļi id. Tu. kamboļi id. Te kambaļamu, kambaļi, kambadi id., rug, woollen cloth. Pa. kambra blanket. Ga. (Oll.) kambal id. Go. (W) kamrá id. Kur. kamrā id. Malt. kamri id. Br. kambal id. /Skt. kambala(ka) woollen blanket or cloth or upper garment. Pa. Pkt. kambala- id. H. kamlī, kămrī, kambal id. Turner, s.v. kamlo.

Ta. kampu post, stake, pole, rod, stick, branch of tree; kampi beam, slender post; kampam post, pillar. Ma. kampu rod, stick; kampam pillar, mast, post. Ko. kab stone pillar, post fixed in ground at Kolme'l village. To. kob post. Ka. kamba post, pillar, mast. Kod. kambi pillar. Tu. kamba, kamma pillar, post. Te. kambamu column. /Skt. (Ved.) skambha pillar, support. Pa, Pkt. khambha- id. Turner, S. v. khāmo. id., DICTIONARY 21 one

Ta. kammi deficiency, scantiness. Ma. kammi id. Ko. kamy a little; kamycdanm inferiority. Ka. kammi deficiency. Kod. kammi small, little, short. Tu. kammi deficient, defective. (H. kami littleness, scantiness, deficiency (< Pers.)

Ta. karmam, karumam action, work, deed, fruit of deeds, religious rites. Ma. karmam action, religious act, fate, actions of this and former lives (chiefly bad actions and their consequences). Ko. karm (obl. karm-, kart-) sin; karmn sinful man. Ka. karma, kamma action, business, religious action or rite, sin. Tu. karma action, religious ceremony, fate, sin. Te. karmamu action, religious rite, fate, fruit of actions. Skt. karman- act, action, business, work, religious rite, fate. Pkt. kamma- id. b Ta. kammavar a Telugu agricultural caste. Ka. kamme of the eight brahmanical castes (in Mysore only smārta brāhmaṇas). Te. kamma a certain caste (of Śūdras); kammari woman of the Kamma caste; kamatakādu, kam(m)atīdu, kammatagădu a laborer or slave employed in tillage; kam(m)atamu cultivation, tillage.

Ta. kavați cowry. Ma. kavați, kaviți id., Cypraea moneta. Ka. kavaại, kavadike, kavade cowrie. Kod. kavļi id. Tu. kavadi, kavadigè, kavaçè id. Te. gavva id. Skt. kaparda-, kapardikā- id. Pkt. kavadda-, kavaddiā- id. H. kauſi id. Turner, s.v. kauſi.

Ta. kavāțam a bullock-load of wood or grass or straw. Ka. kavāda, kabada a bullock- or horse-load of grass, wood, etc. Te. kabādamu a bullock-load of grass or straw. /H. kabār a load or bundle of grass, firewood, etc.

Ta. kavunțan caste title of certain Tamil and Kanarese folk; kavță head of a village. Ma. (Godavarma) gavuņțan a class title of certain Tamil and Kanarese folk. Ko. gavſ important man, headman; gavņdky headman (< Badaga). To. kofdky guestmaster of Badaga village. Ka. gavuşa, gauņa, gavada chief officer of a village; a good caste of peasants; gavudike business of a gavuda; gavudi female servant. Kod. gavși servant-girl (< Ka.). Tu. gaude, gauda, gauņde headman of a village; man of a caste of farmers; gauņi, gauņși female servant. Te. gauņdu honorific title of a class of Sudras. /Mar. gāvdā inferior officer in a village; a particular caste (< Skt. grāma-kūțachief of a village [belonging to the sūdra caste); Pkt. gāmaŭda- id. (DNM]).
Te. gadda, gradda kite. Kol. gadda id. Nk. gadda vulture. Pa. gadda id. Go. (Koya) gada id.; (A) gandal kite. /Skt. gỉdhravulture. Pa. gaddha- id. Pkt. gaddha-, giddha- id.

Ta. kani mine. Ma. khani id. Ka. kaņi, gani, gani ditch, 22 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN basin, mine. Kod. kanatare, kantare well. Tu. kaņi ditch, trench. Te. gani mine, quarry, excavation. /Skt. khani- mine, quarry.

Ta. kanni virgin, young unmarried woman, youthfulness, virginity, state of being earliest in time; kannimai virginity. Ma. kanni virgin. Ko. kan (kan pemog virgin, young childless woman; ka(n) na.g buffalo before it has been bred; kan garc cow at first calving; kan vi'r first pregnancy; kan ge v cow's first calf; kan mog woman's first child). Ka. kanne girl, maiden, virgin. Kod. kanni virgin, unmarried girl; kaññi girl. Te. kanniya, kanne unmarried girl, virgin; young, fresh. /Skt. kanya- girl, virgin. Pa. kaññā- id. Pkt. kaņņā-, kannā id.

Ta. kākitam, kāyitam paper, epistle. Ma. käkittam, kāyitam paper. Ko. ka gydm (obl. ka gydt-), ka'ydm (obl. ka'ydt-) paper. Ka. . kāgada, kāgaja, kāgida paper, epistle. Kod. ka gïda letter. Tu, kāgaji, kākaji paper, letter. Te. kākitamu, kāgitamu, kāyitamu paper. Kuwi (S) kāgitomi id. H. kāgad, kāgaz paper, etc. (< Pers.).

Ta. kāņam oil-press K Ka.). Ka. gāna oil-mill, sugarcane press or mill; gāṇiga oil-miller. Tu. gāna oil-mill, sugarmill; gāņige oil-miller. Te. gānūga oil-mill, sugar-mill. / H. ghānā oil-mill; Mar. ghāņā block on which the roller of a mill moves, oil-mill (< Pkt. ghāņamill < ghāana- slaughter < Skt. ghātana- striking). Turner, s.v. ghān.
Ta. kāņțam stem, stalk. Ma. kāņțam id. Ka. kāņda id. Te. kāda id., stick, handle, shaft. Kui kānļi, kāndru stem, stalk. Skt. kāņda- stem, stalk.
Ta. kāņțam curtain, cloth, garment. Ka. kāņda curtain. curtain. /Skt. kāņda-pața- outer tent, curtain.

Ta. kāyam wound, contusion. Ma. kayam a wound. Ko. ka'ym id., slash, mark. Ka. gaya a bruise, wound. Kod. ga'ya a wound. Tu. ghāya id. Te. gāyamu id., injury, bruise. Pa. gåva a wound. /Skt. ghata- a blow, bruise, wound. Pkt. ghāa- id. H. ghāv id. Mar. ghāy, ghāv id. Turner, s.v. ghāu.

Ta. kārațam, kāruțam jugglery; kārațan, kāruțan juggler. Ka. garada, gāradi, gāruda, gāruļi, gāļi conjuring, jugglery; gārudiga conjurer, juggler. Te. gāradamu, gārađĩ, gārudamu jugglery, trickery; gāradidu juggler. /Skt. gāruda- relating to Garuda; cf. gārudikacharmer, dealer in antidotes. Mar. gāruļī, garodi a snake charmer; juggler, conjurer,

Ta. karaṇam cause, origin; kāraṇan the Supreme Being; chief, ruler; kāraṇavan God. Ma. kāranam cause, origin; kāranan author, originator; man of authority; kāraṇavan head of family, hereditary predecessor; the maternal uncle. Ko. kaóranm (obl. ka'rant-) Kod. a cause. DICTIONARY 23 ka roņë, ka•roņavën ancestor; (M. N. Srinivas, Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India) kāraṇava the apotheosized spirit of the dead ancestor of a Coorg okka. Skt. kāraṇa- cause, origin.

Ka. gārige a flat cake made of wheaten or rice flour and jaggory, and fried in ghee or oil. Tu. gårige a kind of cake or fritter. Te. gāre, gharika a kind of cake. /Pkt. ghāriā- 'miştānna' - Guj. ghari a kind of sweetmeat, a kind of pastry of circular form; Skt. ghārika- (v.l. ghārikā-) Matsyapurāņa (ed. ASS) 63. 19.

Ta. kāriyam result, action, affair, business, object, purpose. Ma. kāryam business, duty, matter. Ko. kaörye'v (obl. kaörye'v-, ka rye.t-) affair, business, aim. To. ko'rym ceremony, rituals and rules to be observed by priest. Ka. kārya, kāriya, kāre affair, business, a festal occasion, effect, motive, cause. Tu. kārya work, business, ceremony, cause, effect. Te. kāryamu work, business, affair, effect, profit, motive, (K also) auspicious occasion, nuptials. Skt. kāryawork, business, religious performance, result, effect, motive, object, purpose.

Ta. karai mortar, plaster for building, concretions that encrust the teeth. Ka. gāre a dilute mixture of earth, lime, etc., to be used as mortar. Tu. gārè, kāre lime plaster. Te. gāra mortar, plaster, cement. (H. Mar. gārā plaster, mortar, Turner, s. v. gāro?.

Ta. kārttikai Pleiades; the 8th lunar month, October-November. Ma. kārttika Pleiades; the 8th lunar month. To. ka:ștk Pleiades. Ka. kārtika the 8th lunar month. Tu. kārtika id. Te. kārtikamu id. /Skt. kārttikan. pr. month.

Ta. kālam, kālai time, season, opportune moment; kāl time; bloom, freshness, beauty; turn. Ma. kālam time, season, year; kāl time. Ko. ka•lm (obl. ka.lt-) time, opportunity. To. ko‘lm (obl. ko.lt-) time; mun go'stk in ancient times. Ka. kala time, year, season; kāl time, opportunity. Kod. ka'la year. Tu. kāla time, season. Te. kalamu id., opportunity. /Skt. kala time, etc.

Ta. kāvatam, kåtam an Indian league, about 10 miles. Ma. kātam = about 5 miles. Ka. gāvada, gāvuda an Indian league, from 10 to 12 miles. Tu. gāvuda a stage or distance of 12 miles. Skt. gavyūti - 2 krosas. Pa. gāvuta- id.

Ta. kiţiki window. Ma. kiţikki, kuțukki id. Ka. kidaki, kidiki, kițaki, kiţiki id., wicket. Kod. kïạike window. Tu. kiţiki id. Te. kiţiki id. Skt. khatakkika-, khadakkikā- side door. Pkt. khadakkiid., window. H. khiệkī, Mar. khidki id. Turner, s.v. khirki.

Ta. kițſam lump of metal, sediment, coating, crust, scoria, state a COSS 24 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN worm. a renown. of being dry and hard. Ma. kițțam dross, scoria. Ko. kit hard lump of earth. Ka. kiţța dirt, dross of iron, dregs, rust. Tu. kițța scoria, dross of smelted iron, sediment of boiled areca-nut. Skt. kițța- dirt, rust of iron. Pkt. kițţa- rust. Turner, s.v. kit.

Ta. kīțam worm, maggot, vermin. Ma. kitam Ka. kidi, kita worm, insect. Tu. kidụ, kidi, kīța id. Te. cīda, cida-purugu certain parasitic worm causing disease in plants and animals, (B) a caterpillar or worm that destroys plants, a grub inside a fruit or a seed; kitamu worm, insect. Skt. kīța- worm, insect. Pkt. kida-, kīdaaid. Turner, s.v. kiro.

Ta. kirttanam, kirtti praise, fame, glory; kirttanai praise, song; cirtti Ma. kırttanam, kirtti praise. Ko. ki•rt, kiirty, ki•rtanm (obl. ki'rtant-) disgrace. Ka. kīrti, kiriti, kirtana praise, fame; kirtane song of praise. Tu. kirti fame; kirtanè praise, hymn. Te. kirti fame; kirtana praise, song of praise; kirtanamu praise. Skt. kirti- mentioning, good report, fame, glory; kirtana- mentioning, telling; kirtana- id., fame; (from 'telling,' Ko. has 'evil report' rather than 'good report').

Ta. kunkulu, kunkiliyam, kukkuluvam various Shorea and Balsamodendron (Amyris) species. Ma. kunkuliyam, kurkkilam the bdellium tree. Ka. guggulu, guggula, guggaļa, guggiļa, gugguļa, gurguļa bdellium, Amyris agallochum, Moringa hyperanthera, Boswellia serrata, var, glabra Roxb. Tu. gugguļa bdellium, Boswellia glabra. Te. guggilamu resin of Shorea robusta. /Skt. guggulu-, gulgulu- bdellium or the exudation of Amyris agallochum. [(1) Balsamodendron Roxburghii Arn. (?) Amyris agallocha Roxb. (2) Boswellia serrata Roxb.; B. serrata, var. glabra B. glabra Roxb. (3) Moringa pterygosperma Gaertn. Hyperanthera moringa Vahl. (4) Shorea robusta Gaertn.)

Ka. gunța, gūņța, kūța peg, plug; gudida id., stumpy post. Kod. gu'ța peg, post. Tu. gũnța, guņķi, gunțè, güņtigè peg, pin, stake. Te. gūțamu stake, post, peg; gudide hinge, peg, pivot. Go. (Sironcha) kuțța pillar, post. Pkt. khunța- peg. H. khūtā stump, stake, post, peg; . Mar. khūță, khūți stake, peg. Turner, s.v. khuţțo, khuțți.

Ta. kuttakai contract of lease. Ma. kuttaka farm, contract (as for liquor, honey, wax), monopoly. Ko. guti'g government contract. Ka. guttă, gutte exclusive right of sale, farm, monopoly; guttige id., rental on land. Tu. guttige liquor-shop; guttedāre holder of a monopoly, a liquor contractor, Te. gutta lease. [Skt. kuttā a type of 'farminglease' in South India (J. Duncan M. Derrett, BSOAS 21.61-81). H. guttā exclusive right of sale, monopoly, contract, lease. Or. kuta appraisement of the produce of a field, tree, or tank (ib. 62, n. 2). Derrett takes = khũți peg. DICTIONARY 25 manure. the words to be Dravidian in origin, since the legal institution is South Indian.

Ta. kuppācam coat, bodice, jacket. Ma. kuppayam jacket, gown, robe. Ko. kupa'cm (kupa ct) coat, men's special dancing dress with full skirt. To. kuposm (kupost-) coat. Ka. kuppasa, kub(b)asa, kubusa jacket. Kod. kuppia Coorg man's coat. Tu. kuppasa petticoat, bodice. Te. kup(p)asamu, kubusamu, (K also) kūsamu half-jacket, woman's bodice. Kol. kubasam bodice. Nk. kubaśam id. /Skt. kůrpása- cuirass, quilted jacket worn as armor; kūrpāsaka- bodice, jacket (worn esp. by women), cuirass, corselet. Pkt. kuppāsa-, kuppisa- id. (P. Thieme, ZDMG 91.90f., 92.52; H. W Bailey, Donum natalicum H. S. Nyberg oblatum 10f.).

Ta. kuppi cowdung. Ko. ko.ba:rm (obl. ko ba.rt-) To. kuborm (obl. kubort-) id. Ka. gobbara id. Tu. gobbara id.; ? kurpu id. Te. gobbaramu id.; (K also) gobbi a lump of cowdung worshipped as a goddess. Skt. go(r)vara- cowdung. Pkt, gov(v)ara- id. H. gobar fresh cowdung. Mar. govar Mar. govar dry cowdung. Turner, s.v. gobar.

Ta. kuppi vial, bottle. Ma. kuppi vial, bottle (chiefly of crystal). Ka. kuppi, kuppige vial, bottle. Kod. kuppi piece of glass, bottle. Tu. kuppi glass-ware, china-ware, bottle. Te. kuppe jar, bottle. Kui kupi an earthenware pot with a long, narrow neck and mouth, a goblet. /H. kuppi leather bottle for oil or ghee, vial. Turner, s.v. kuppā, kuppi.

Ta. kumpakāran potter. Ma. kumbhakaran id. To. kumo'rn id. Ka. kumbhakāra, kumbagāra, kumbāra, kumbara id. Kod. kumba:rë id.; stupid fellow. Tu. kumb e, kumbāre, kumbare potter Te. kumbhakārūdu, kummari id. Pa. kummal id. Go. (Muria, etc.) kummal id. Kui kumbarenju id.; fem. kumbareri. Kuwi (F) kümbra, (s) kumbra potter. /Skt. kumbhakāra potter. Pkt. kumbhaara-, kumbhara id. H. kumhār, Mar. kūbhär id. Turner, s. v. kumäle.

Ta. kulam family, caste, genus, flock. Ma. kulam flock, family, Ko. kolm, golm caste, species, kind. To. kwasm genus (esp. of buffaloes); sacred name (of all things mentioned in prayers and songs); kwalm thing. Ka. kula herd, race, family, caste. Tu. kula family, race, tribe. Te. kulamu, kolamu caste, race, tribe, family, class. Kui klāmbu (pl. klāpka) family, lineage, kin, tribe, race, nationality, sort, species, variety, kind; kūlu family, clan, tribe, caste. Skt. kula- herd, race, family, caste.

Ta. kēţțai the 18th nakşatra; goddess of misfortune. Ma. kēțța the 18th lunar asterism. To, keot a heavenly body bringing misfortune. race. 26 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 1 a Ka. jyēşthe, jēșțe, jēțe the 18th lunar mansion; goddess of misfortune. Tu. jyēșthe, jēştè misfortune, calamity. Te. jyėștha the 18th lunar mansion; elder sister of Lakshmi, the goddess of misfortune and poverty. /Skt. jyeșthā- the 18th lunar mansion; misfortune, personified as the elder sister of Lakşmi.

Ta. kēvu, kēvu, kērvu charge for transporting goods by sea, freight. Ma. kēvu, kēļi freight, passage money; kēvi shipper; kēļikka to freight. Tu. kēvu boat-hire. Te. kēvu freight. H. khewā ferryfare. Turner, s. v. khewāl (< Skt. kşepa-).

Ta. kēļi fun, jest, joke, ridicule, mimicry; kēļi, kēļikkai women's sport. Ma. kēli play, sport. Ko. geryļ, gey! sport, jest, amorous sport. To. ke‘ly mockery. Ka. gēli ridicule, derision. Tu. gēli ridicule, jest, mockery, insult. Te. gēli ridicule, mockery, joking. Skt. keliplay, sport, amorous sport, amusement. L. V.R. 1934. 263.
Ta. kottam costus root. Ma. koțțam Costus speciosus; Ocimum petiolare Rh. /Skt. kuştha- c. speciosus or arabicus. Pa. koţthaplant, ? c. speciosus. (C. speciosus Smith - C. arabicus Jacq.)

Ta. koțțāram granary, place where grains are husked, elephant stall, palace; koțțakāram, koțțu granary; koțțați storeroom, cattleshed. Ma. koțțāram, koțțakāram stable, place where temple affairs are managed, palace. Ka. koţțāra storeroom, treasury; koțāra threshing floor. Tu. koțţāra palace, storeroom. Te. koțțu, koțțați storehouse, shop; koțāramu, koțāru storehouse, magazine. Skt. koştha-, koșthāgāragranary, storeroom, treasury. Pkt. koţtha-, kotthā(g)āra-, koțțhāra- id. Mar, kothār granary; kothời storeroom.

Ta. kottamalli, kottamuri coriander, Coriandrum sativum. Ma. kottampalari id. Ka. kot(t)ambari, kot(t)umbari, kottiri, kottumari, kottumiri id. Tu. kottambari, kottamberi, kottembari, kottumbri id. Te. kot(t)imiri coriander plant or leaves. /Skt. kustumbari-, kustumburucoriander. Pkt. kutthumbhari- id:
Ka. godde Te. gudda /Skt. guda-
Ta. kopparam elbow. Ka. koppara shoulder-blade. Te. kopparamu shoulder. Ga. (Oll.) kopre elbow. Skt. kūrpara- elbow. Pkt. koppara- id.

Ta. koyyā, koyyal guava, Psidium guyava. Ma. koyyā-maram guava tree. Ka. koyyā guava, P. pyriferum L. Te. (B) goyyā-pandu guava fruit. From a South American language through Portuguese; see Dalgado-Soares, Portuguese Vocables in Asiatic Languages, s. v. goiabo; Hobson-Jobson, s.v. guava; neither really explains the forms recorded. (P. guyava Linn.; P.g., var. pyriferum Linn. Not indigenous to India.) anus. anus. anus. DICTIONARY 27 a score. Score. score.

Ka. golla, gollaļa cowherd. Kod. gollë man of cultivator caste. Tu. golle man of the cowherd or milkman caste. Te. golla caste of shepherds and herdsmen; a watchman, guard; gollāļu, gollavādu herdsman, shepherd; fem gollata, golladi. Mar. (Kulkarni) gol = gop cowherd. Cf. the various IA forms in Turner, s. v. gwālo.
Ga. (Oll.) göra horse. Go. kõļā id. Kui gõſa id. Kuwi (S) gõda id. Kur. ghoro id.; ghori mare. Malt. goro horse. /Skt. ghoțaka- horse. H. ghoſā, Mar. ghodā id. Turner, s.v. ghoſā.

Ta. kõți a score (as in counting precious stones, silk, etc.). Ma. kõți, kõțța Tu. köại id. Te. kõdiga id. (used chiefly in counting precious stones). Kui kõſie twenty. Kuwi (F) koreka, (S) kādi id. Kur, kuri Malt. kóși id. H. korī, Mar. kodi Turner, s.v. kori?.

Ta. kõtumai, kötumpai, koti wheat, Triticum vulgare. Ma. kõtampu, kõtampam. Ko. go dym, go dymb. To. kwï.Diby. Ka. godi, gödive, gödume, göduve. Ko. go.due (? go dve). Tu. godi, gödhi. Te. göd(h)uma. Kol. godma. Kol. godma. Nk. godma. Pa. gong. Go, gohk (pl.), (Pat.) gohku. Kui gohomo. Kui gohomo. Kuwi (S) gohonga. Kur. gohom. Malt. gohme. Br. khólum. Skt. godhūma- wheat. Pkt. gohūma- id. Bihari gohum, gohũ id. Turner, s.v. gahū.

Ta. komaram inspiration, possession by spirits. Ma. komaram oracle of a god, possessed devil-dancer. Skt. kumāra- boy, son, Skanda. Pkt. kumăra- id. The secondary derivative Skt. kaumāra-, Pkt. komāra- (also komara-), here means 'possessed by Skanda (Ta. murukan):
Ta. kõli jujube tree. Ma. kõlam jujuba. Ka. kola the fruit of jujube; kõli jujube tree, Zizyphus jujuba Lam. /Skt. koli- id.; kola- jujube fruit. C, J

Ta. akkulli, cakkulli a steamed meal-cake. Ka. cakkali, cakkuli, cakli, cakkuļi a ring of paste without sugar, but with a little salt, etc., fried in ghee or oil. Tu. cakkuli a cake made of rice flour, salt, etc., and fried in oil, Te. cakkilamu a kind of cake. Skt. śaskulĩ-, śaskulħa large round cake of ground rice, sugar, and sesamum, cooked in oil. Pkt. sakkuli- id. DED 2055 suggests with much uncertainty a Dravidian origin for the IA words. 28 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 1 a
Ta, cakațu, cakațai, cākāțu, cāļu cart. Ma. cakațu, cāļu covered car. Ka. cak(k)adā, cakkadi cart. . Te. cekadā id. /Skt. śakața-, sakați- cart. Pkt. sagadi-, saada-, sāļi- id.

Ta. caki (-pp-, -tt-) to bear, tolerate, excuse, forgive; cakippu bearing, enduring, forgiving; cakippāļi one who bears with patience, one who forgives. Ma. sahikka to bear, endure, forgive. Ka. sahisu, sairisu, sayrisu to bear, bear patiently, suffer, endure, be patient, put up with, be able to bear up against; sairane, sayrane patience, endurance, bearing; sõsu to endure, bear. Tu. sahisuni, sayisuni to bear, endure, suffer, forgive; sairipuni, sairisuni to bear, endure, suffer; sairane patience, endurance. Te, saīcu to bear, endure, pardon, excuse, forgive; be agreeable, tasty (as food); saīpu, saſpudu, (K also) sayipu bearing, endurance; sairaņa patience, forgiveness; sairincu to be patient, endure, suffer, bear. /Skt. sah to bear, endure, tolerate, have patience with.

Ka. jagala a quarrel, fight, war. Kod. jagala a quarrel. Tu. jagaļa, jagaļāța, jaguļu quarrel, fight, dispute. Te. jagadamu a quarrel, dispute, fight, altercation, battle; vb. jagadam-āļu; jagașincu to quarrel, fight. Pkt. jhagada- quarrel. H. jhagrā id. Mar. jhagdā, jhagad id.; jhagadņē to quarrel. Turner, s. v. jhagaſă.

Ta. cankațam ferryboat of two canoes with a platform thereon (said to be < Ptg. jangada); cankāļam a kind of boat; cankuvațam ferryboat (said to be < Ptg. jangada). Ma. cannātam ferryboat, made of two boats. Ka. jangāl platform on two boats, used at ferries. Tu. jangălų, jangāru wooden platform placed on boats. Skt. samghāța- joining of timber. Pa. sanghāța- union, raft. Pkt. samghāda- pair, couple. Mar. săgad double-canoe. Sgh. hanguļuva, aŭguļa id. Turner, s.v. sanāri. Periplus váyyapov. Ptg. jangada, for which see Dalgado-Soares, Portuguese Vocables in Asiatic Languages. Also see Hobson-Jobson, s. w. jancada, jangar.

Ta. cañkili chain, link, fetter. Ma. cannala chain; cannu small chain to which to hang keys. Ko. caŋgyl chain; tega'l, tega lg door-chain. To. tagas chain (in poetry: ka(s) tegas stone chain (in the story of chaining the sun); pï(n) tegas gold chain); tokwal leg chains (of elephant; in poetry); prison, sentence to prison. Ka. śşńkhala, śộnkhale, sankale, sańkole iron chain, any chain or fetter; chain for confining the feet of an elephant. Kod. caŋŋo•le chain. Tu. sankale, sankõlè id., fetter. Te. sankela id. Kol. sakri chain. Pa. cakril id. Go. (W) sánkar id. Kui sikal, sikali id. Kuwi (F) hikri, (S) hikni, hikli id. /Skt. śřńkhală - chain. Pkt. sank(h)ală- id. H. sãkal, sãkar, sãkrī, sīkar, sikal. Turner, s.v. sānlo. a DICTIONARY 29

Ka. sajjige, sajjaka, sojjige, sõji wheaten flour in fine granules, wheaten grits, rolong; grits of roasted rice, a mess or dish made of grits of roasted rice. Tu. sajjige, sojjigè, sõji rolong or wheaten grits. Te. sojje, (B also) sojji rice boiled after being roasted. /H. Mar. soji id. Turner, s.v. suji.

Ka. saņal(u), saņil(u), sadlu to become loose, become slack, relax, become lax; caus. sadalisu, saờilisu, sadilcu, sadlisu; sad(a)la, sad(a)lu, sadila, saờilu, salla, sallu the state of being loose, slack, relaxed, or lax. Kod. sadala looseness. Tu. sadily loose, slack, loosened. Te. sadalu to become loose or slack, be loosened; n. looseness, slackness; sadalincu, sadal(u)cu to loosen, untie. /Pkt. sadhila-, siļhilaloose (cf. Skt. śithila- id.). Cf. Burrow, The Sanskrit Language 45 f. Cf. entry 183, Ka. dilla.

Ka. jadi, jidi a long-continued, fine, small rain. Tu. jadipini, jadipuni, jadiyuni to rain incessantly. Te. jadi rain. Malt. jara rain. | Pkt. jhadi- continuous rain (DNM). Mar. jhaời long-continued rain. H. jhaf heavy shower. Turner, s.v. jhari.

Ta. (Irawati Karve, Kinship Organisation in India 201) cațțakan wife's sister's husband. Ka. saddaka a man who has become the relation of another by marrying the sister of that man's wife. Tu. sadduke the relation in which the husbands of two sisters stand to each other. Te. saddakūdu a fellow son-in-law. Kui sadu the husband of a wife's sister. Turner, s.v. sāſu.

Ta. caņți wicked man or woman; obstinate, perverse person. Ma. canți obstinate, stubborn. Ko. candy man who will not listen to advice. Ka. candi an obstinate man; obstinacy. Tu. canda vehemence, obstinacy; vehement, obstinate, quarrelsome. Te, caņdi obstinate, stubborn; an obstinate person. /Skt. canda- fierce, violent, cruel, passionate.

Ka. sanna, sanna small, tiny, thin, delicate, slender; smallness, etc. Kod. canna, sanna small. Te. sanna, sannani, sannamu thin, slender, narrow, fine, gentle, not loud; sannana thinness, smallness, narrowness, fineness. Skt. ślakṣṇa- slippery, smooth, tender, small. Pkt. sanha-, sanha smooth, small. Turner, s.v. sānu.
Ta. caturam square; caturi (-pp-, -tt-) to cut or make a square figure. Ma. caturam square. Ko. cadrm (obl. cadrt-) a square, a Te, cadaramu square (n. and adj.). Skt. catur- four.

Ta. canti joint, etc.; cantu joint, hips, road-crossing, narrow street, lane, gap, crack, cleft. Ma. cantu joint, cleft; sandhu joint, limb; canti buttocks, posteriors; sandhi union, joint, vulva. Ko. cand joint; narrow path between houses. To. sod joint. Ka. sandhi, sandi cross. 30 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN joint, etc.; sandu juncture, joint, lane, cleft, fissure. Kod. candi anus; vulva. Tu. sandhi union, juncture, etc.; sandy, sandu cleft, joint. Te. sandu narrow street, lane, corner, opening, fissure, crack, hole. Skt. samdhi- junction, joint, interstice, crevice, vulva. L. V.R. 1935, 74.

Ta. cantai a fair, market, Shandy, bazaar, multitude. Ma. canta a fair, weekly or annual market. Ko. caynt market. To. soty market day; week. Ka. sante, santi assemblage, fair or market, market-place. Kod. catte market. Tu. santé id., fair. Konda sata village market. Skt. samsthā- assembly (lex.; but cf. BHS samsthāgāra-, Pa. samthāgāraassembly hall); Pkt. *samthă-. Cf. also Skt. samsthāna- public place in a town, Pa. saņthāna- meeting place, market. The etymology usually given is Skt. samdhā-, which does not have the meaning 'assembly' (though samdhāna- does).

Ta. cappańkam, cappanki sappan-wood, Caesalpinia sappan. Ma. cappannam id. Ka. Sappanga-mara id. Tu. cappanga id. /Said to be < Malay sěpang or Minangkabau sapang; but Hooker takes the tree to be native in India as well as in 'Malay isles.' Hobson-Jobson (s. v. sappan-wood) suggests that the tree is indigenous in Mababar, Deccan, and Malay Peninsula and the name good Dravidian, whence Indonesia has borrowed.

Ta. capparam canopied vehicle or small car on wheels in which idols are carried during festivals, testered bedstead. Ma. capparam shed or thatch, litter of an idol and place where it is kept. To. soporm shed. Ka. cappara frame thrown over houses to form the roof, shed, thatched or tiled roof, canopy of a bedstead. Tu. cappara shed, pandal. Te. capparamu canopied seat in which an idol is carried about, shed or pandal, canopy of a bed. (H. chappar thatched roof, hut (< Skt. chattvarahouse, bower). Turner, s.v. chāpro.

Ta. campaļam provisions for journey; wages, salary. Ma. campa- ļam, śampalam wages, salary. wages, salary. Ko. cambaļm id. To. sobulm id. Ka. sambaļa provender for journey; pay, salary (monthly or yearly). Tu. sambala pay, salary, wages. Te. sambalamu, sambalamu, sambadamu id. /Skt. sambala- provisions for a journey. Turner, s.v. sāmal.

Ta. campaļi betel pouch, bag, wallet. Ka. sambalige a covered box made of õle. Te. sambaļika, sambela wallet, satchel, esp. for holding betel leaves, nuts, etc. Skt. sampuța(ka)-, sampuţikā- box, casket.
Kod. jams- (jamsi -) to utter (incantation). Tu. jamipuni id. Skt. jalp- to mutter, say. Pkt. jamp- id.

Ta. carākai metal cup (loc.); caruvam shallow, wide-mouthed vessel. To. tarx bronze food vessel. Ka. caravige, carivige, carvige, а 1 DICTIONARY 31 cavarige, cavurige a large copper or brass pot in the form of a cambu for carrying water; carige, cerige id.; (= cambu) a globular copper or glass vessel, used for drinking water. Tu. carige a cooking utensil of copper or brass. Te. cerava, ceravamu a brass kettle or boiler. Skt. saraka- drinking vessel; sarāva(ka)- shallow cup, plate, platter; there seems to have been contamination or development of meaning.

Ta. cari similarity, suitability, agreement, exactness, rightness, propriety, regularity, equal measure or quantity; yes, right. Ma. sari, sari even, like, equal, right, correct. Ko. cery equal, good, right, correct; cerya'n excellent, beautiful, clever, very. To. sary right, correct; height. Ka. sari the state or condition of being adjusted, fitness, propriety, suitableness, rightness, correctness, evenness, sameness, similarity, equality, an equal thing, fit, proper, right, reasonable; vb. to put in proper order, adjust; sarikatana equality of position; sariga an equal, a man of equal power; saru sameness, equality. Kod. sëri correct. Tu. sari equal, like; just, right, proper, fit, even, not odd, full; interj. very good; sarike right, fit, proper, level, even, abundant, complete; sarta straight, direct; sarāriyuni to be exact; sarāsari equally, alike, right, proper, on average. Te. sari equal, equivalent, suitable, fit, proper, corresponding, similar, like, just like, reasonable, correct, right, faultless, straight, level, even, flat, not odd, completed, equality, similarity, etc.; yes, all right; (K also) sar(u)du, sarusu to distribute equally, (coll.) economize. Kui sarna straight, outstretched, upright. Kur. to put in its proper place, stow. Malt. saryare to be cured, be ready; saryatre to cure, mend, correct. Br. ? shar good, beautiful; well, properly (also Bal.). Skt. sadṛśa- like, resembling, suitable, fit. Pkt. sari- id.

Ka. cala dazzle; caļacaļa, calacaļane dazzlingly; jalakkane, jalarkane, jalak(k)ane clearly, purely, brightly, shiningly; clearness, etc. Tu. caļacaļa glittering; jalujaly brightly; jalakų glitter, gleam; jalakuni to shine; jalakāvuni to cause to shine. /Mar. jha!ak, jhaljha! glitter. Turner, s. vv. jhalak, jhalkanu, jhaljhal.

Ta. callā muslin; cēlai cloth, saree. Ma. sallāvu muslin; callā cloth without a border, as muslin; cēla cloth, esp. of women. Ka. śalya, śalle muslin cloth without a border; cēla, salya, śalle, selle, śēle, sēle cloth, clothes, garment. Kod. ce le belt, sash worn by Kodagu man. Tu. śalya, śallè, sēlè, cēlè a thin upper cloth, generally without border. Te. sellä a cloth without a border; cēla, cēlamu cloth, clothing. Skt. cela clothes, garment. Mar. sela a sort of robe. Cf. DED entry 2161, and Mayrhofer, s. v. celam. sarya'ānā 32 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN Tu. jalli a

Ta. calli short pendant in ornaments, hangings. Ka. jalli, jhalli tassels, hangings, a whisk made of the tail of the camara. chaplet of flowers, flowers dangling down the head, etc., anything dangling or hanging loosely. Te. jalli a whisk, tassel. [Cf. Mar. jhālar, jhallar fringe, etc.; jhāl tassel; jhaļam that hangs dangling and waving in the wind. Turner, s. v. jhālar.
Ka. jalli, jalle large round bamboo basket used for storing corn. Te. jalla a long narrow basket placed on a cart for carrying grain. /H. jhāl, jhalla, jhalli large basket. Turner, s.v. jhālar.

Ta. calli falsehood (< Te.); callikkaran liar, hypocrite. Ka. jalli falsehood, a lie; jala fraud, hypocrisy; jalika a deceiver. Tu. jalli boast, bragging; jalliyuni to boast, brag. Te. jalli falsehood, false; jallikādu a liar. H. ja'i forgery; jaʻli forged, counterfeit, false, spurious (< Ar.).

Ta. cavaļam bearded dart or lance, pike. Ma. cavalam lance, a bearded javelin. Ka. sabaļa spear, lance, pike (one of the tatsamas). Te. sabalamu a kind of spear. /Skt. sarvalā-, śarvala an iron club or crowbar. Pkt. savvala-, sabbala- spear. Turner, s. v. såbal.

Ta. cavu (-pp-, -tt-) to fall in price, become cheap, be unsaleable, have no demand; cavukkai cheapness; cavutam id., old stock of goods lying unsold. Ka. cavuka cheap. Te, cavuka, cauka cheapness; cheap. /Mar. savãg cheap; savõgņē to become cheap (< Skt. samarghacheap; Turner, s.v. sahango).

Ta. cavukkam square piece of cloth, towel. Ka. cavuka, cauka, cauku a small uncolored square handkerchief. Kod. cavka long white headdress worn by women at funeral; the modern long headdress of women. Te. caukamu a square, a towel that is square. Skt. catuṣka consisting of four, square. Pkt. caükka- id. Turner, S. v. cok.

Ka. jāyi, jāji, jādi, jā mace, nutmeg (Myristica moschata Thunb.); Jasminum grandiflorum Lin. Tu. jāji J. grandiflorum; jāji-kāyi -the nutmeg. Te. jāji, jādi id. Skt. jāti- mace, nutmeg; J. grandiflorum. Pkt. *jādi-, jāi- id. (M. fragrans Houtt. M. moschata Thunb. Native to the Eastern Moluccas.)

Ta. căți (-pp-, -tt-) to slander; chide, reprove; n. malicious report, slander; câțu (cāți- ) to abuse, reprove. Ka. câţi, câda, cahada slander; cāda slanderer; fem, cāļi; jādisu . to reprove. Kod. ca di talebearing, information laid against someone. Tu. cāļi slander; cāļiyuni to slander. Te. cāļĩ backbiting. /Mar. cahāļ, cāļ a traducer, defamer; cahādi, cāļi defamation, slander.

Ta. cāļi jar, a measure of capacity. Ma. câți jar. Ko. cairy : 1 1 DICTIONARY 33 Tu. prabig basket with wide mouth. To. toʻſy, to·dy broad storage basket. Ka. jādi jar. Tu. jāļi large earthen vessel. Te. jāņi large bottle or jar. /Pa. cāți- jar, waterpot. H. cāți earthen vessel or pitcher. The forms with j- may result from contamination with forms of the H. Mar. group jhāri water-pot with spout; cf. Turner, s.v. jhāri?.
Ta. cāņakam, cānam, cāņi cowdung. Ma. cāņakam, cānam, cāņi id. Kod. caiņa id. Skt. chagana- dried cowdung. dried cowdung. Pkt. chagana-, *chaaņa-, chāna- id. Mayrhofer, s. v. chaganaḥ.

Ta. cāņai, cāņai-kkal grindstone, whetstone. Ma. cāņa id. Ko. ca'n sharpness (of razor, knife), smoothness (of ground spice); ca'n kal whetstone. Ka. sāņe, sāņe-kal grindstone, whetstone. Tu. sāņè, sāņekallu id. Te. sāna id. Skt. śāņa- whetstone, grindstone.

Ta. catam boiled rice; căppiţu (căppițuv-, cāppiţt-) to eat, drink, consume, misappropriate; căppățu food, meal (esp. of human beings); cāppăţțu-rāman glutton. Ma. śāppāțu a meal of brahmans. sādamu cooked rice. Te. sadamu food, rice; pasādamu, (K also) pasadanamu boiled rice, cooked food; pasāpadu to eat; sāpaļu to eat, , dine; sāpāțu a meal, food. /Skt. prasāda- food presented to god or guru. L. V. Ramaswami Aiyar, IHQ 12.265-6 (also L. V.R. 1935. 67).

Ta. cámi lord, the Supreme Being, chieftain, master, guru, a term of respectful address; cuvāmi id. Ma. sāmi, svāmi id. Ko. co‘ym god. Ka. sāmi, sāyi, sāvi, somi, sõyi, svāmi id. Tu. Sāmi, svāmi id. Te. sāmi, svāmi id. /Skt. svāmin- id. (not the Supreme Being). Pkt. sāmi- id.

Ta. camai common millet, Panicum miliaceum; poor man's millet, P. crusgalli; little millet, P. miliare. Ma. cāma P. miliaceum. Ko. ta'ym millet; ta'ym gu', ta'm gu' cooked millet (ku: cooked rice). To. ta'm ašky husked millet (ašky husked grain, rice). Ka. sāme, save P. frumentaceum. Tu. sāmè millet, P. miliaceum. Te. (K) cama id. Pa. cāma small grain (Halbi gaţkā). Skt. śyāmăka- P. frumentaceum. Pkt. samăa- id. H. sämā, sāwā, săwă id. Mar. sãvā, sāvā id. Turner, s.v. samā?. (P. crus-galli Linn.; P. c., var, frumentaceum - P. frumentaceum Roxb. P. miliaceum Linn. and P. miliare Lamk. have synonymies that "are almost inextricably mixed.")

Ta. сārāyam spirituous liquor, arrack. Ma. сārāyam distilled liquor, wine. To. so'roy spirituous liquor. Ka. sărāya, sărāyi id., arrack. Tu. sārāyi id. Te. sārāya, sārā id. id. Skt. sara essence, nectar.

Ta. ālai apartment, hall, elephant stall or stable; cālai sacrificial or alms hall, school, stable, cow shed, house. Ma. āla shed, work- 34 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN COWshop, cowhouse; śāla hall, house, stable; cāla palace. Ko, a:l shed. To. a's Toda house. Ka. sālā, sāle, sāli, śāle hall, room; school. Tu. sāle, śāle id. Te. sāla house, shed, pandal, hall. Pa. cēla shed. Kuwi (S) hā'la stable, stall, workshop. Skt. śālā- house, hall, shed, stable. Pkt. sālā id. H. sāl house, hall, school. Mar. sāļ workshop. Turner, s.v. -sär3.

Te. jāva gruel, porridge. Pa. cava rice gruel; vār jāva water in which rice has been boiled (cf. DED 4387). Go. jawā porridge, gruel of kõdon and kuțkī; (Pat.) jāwa rice gruel; (W) jáwá penjh (cooked food); (L) jāvā porridge; jāvānā to eat porridge. Konda jāva cooked rice. Kui (P) jau dhal, gravy, soup. /Skt. yavagu- rice-gruel. BHS yvägl-, yāgu- id. Pa. yāgu- id. Turner, s.v. jāulo, esp. Or. jāu overboiled rice, etc.
Ta. cicam lead; iyam white lead, black-lead. Ma. iyam lead. Ko. ti.cl id.; ti cay tin. To. ti'sïl id. Ka. sisa, sisu lead. Tu. sisa id. Te. sisamu id. /Skt. sisa- lead.

Ta. cirakam cumin, Cuminum cyminum. Ma. cirakam id. Ка. jiraka, jīrage, jirige, jīrā id. Tu. jīradari, jīrige id. Te. jirakamu, jīraṇamu, jīlakar(r)a id. Skt. jiraka-, jirana- id. Pkt. jīraa- id. H. jirā id. Turner, s. v. jiro.

Ta, curikai short sword, knife; cūri, cūri-kkatti a kind of sharp knife. Ma. curika dagger, small sword; cūri dagger, knife in a walking stick. Ko, cu'ry flensing knife, two-edged knife. To. tu'ry knife (any kind except billhook). Ka. surige, surigi, suragi knife, dagger; cūri small billhook-like knife. Tu. suriya a demon's straight sword; cūri knife, small sword. Te. suriya, sure knife; cūri, cũra-katti knife. Skt. kşura- razor; kşurikā- knife; chữrikā-, chữri- knife. Pkt. chura-, churi(g)ā-, churi- id. Turner, s. v. churi and App.

Ta. cul littleness, smallness, slenderness; culļalan thin slender man; fem. cullali; culli smallness. Ma. cullu what is little, trifling. /Skt. kşulla- small, minute. Pkt. chulla id. However, there is also Pa. Pkt. culla- id.; see Turner, s.v. chulyāhā.

Ta. cūci, ūci needle. Ma. sūci, tūśi id., iron style. Ko. tu'c needle. Ka. sūci, śūci, sūji, sūje id. Kod. cu di id. Tu. dūji, sūji id., pin. Te. sūci, sūcika, sūdi needle. Kol. su:di id. Nk. sūdi id. Pa. cūcub id. Ga. (Oll.) suja (j = z) id. Konda sūzi id. Kui susi id. Kuwi (F) sūja, (S) sūza (z = j) id. Kur, suſtu, suytu pointed; suyu pointed-nosed; suwa packing-needle. Malt. cúci pointed, sharp. Skt. sūc- needle. Pkt. sui- id. H. sui needle; sūjā packing-needle, awl; sūji needle, small awl. Turner, s. vv. siyo?, sujā. DICTIONARY 35 a

Ta. cūtu gambling. Ma. cūtu id. Ko. cu'jm (obl. cu'jt - ) bet, a race. To. twï'zm (obl. twï.zt-) a bet. Ka. jūdu, jūja, jūju, dyūta gambling. Kod. ju'ji a bet. Tu. jūji, jūju gaming, a wager. Te. . jūjamu, jūdamu gambling. /Skt. dyūta- gambling. Pa. jūta- id. Pkt. *jūda-, jūa- id. Turner, S. v. juwa?.
Ta. cekku oilpress; cekkān, cekkāțti worker of oilpress. Ma. cekkan oilmaker. Ka. cekku oilpress, sugar mill. /Skt. cakra wheel; oil-mill. Pkt. cakka id. Turner, s. v. cāko.
Ka. cejje, cajje, sejje, sajje place of rest or repose, bed. Te. sejja bed, couch. Skt. sayya- bed. Pa. seyyā id. Pkt. sejjā- id. H. sej id.

Ta. cețți vaiśya or mercantile caste, title of traders; fem. cețțicci; cețțimai, ceļļu trade, traffic; etti title of distinction conferred on persons of the Vaiśya caste, the Vaisya caste. Ma. cețți, cettiyan, ettiyān one of the foreign merchant classes; fem. cetticci; cettu trade. To. sity man of Chetti caste (Tamilian). Ka. sețți, sațți, cațți a banker, merchant or tradesman. Te. setti merchant. Skt. śreșthin person of authority, head of a guild. Pa. Pkt. setthi- id., merchant. Cf. H. seth, Guj. śeth head of a guild, banker. Turner, s.v. seth?.
Ta. cețți wrestler, prizefighter. Ka. jețţi, jețtiga, jațți, jattiga professional wrestler. Tu. jețți wrestler. / Mar. jethi id. (< Skt. jyestha-).

Ta. contam one's own peculiar right, exclusive property, near relationship; contakkāran owner, close relation. Ma. Sontam Ko. condm (obl. condt-) close relationship, ownership; one's own; condka.rn, condga'rn owner, close relation. Ka. sonta, svanta belonging to oneself; state of being one's own. Tu. sonta, svanta Те. sontamu own, private. /Skt. sva one's own. Cf. also Pa., BHS santaka- belonging to; ? contamination. S. Anavaratavinayakam Pillai, Dravidic Studies III. 46f., gives other variations and suggests svatantraas the origin; the meaning of the latter is not close, but again contamination is a possibility.

Ka. jompa, jompe cluster, bunch, a mass. Te. jompamu thick foliage, a cluster of leaves, flowers and branches. Pa. joppa bunch, cluster. Kur. jhopā cluster or bunch (fruit, flowers, etc.), ball of thread. Malt. jopa, jopeli bunch, cluster. / H. jhõpā bunch, cluster. Turner, s. v. jhuppo.

Ta. cóți, cāļu a pair, similarity; cõți (-pp-, -tt-) to arrange, adorn. Ma. jõțu, cóțu a pair. Ko. jo'ry id. ; jo'șc- (jo rc-) to put on (jewelry). To. twï'ſ, swi'd a pair. Ka. jõdu, joļi union, a pair, equality, own. own. 36 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN sameness; jõạisu to join, unite; collect; assemble; get ready. Kod. jo:ļi pair. Tu. joļi, jāļu pair; equal, like; jodiyuni to be joined; jõdipuni to join, unite. Te. jõdu, jāņā pair; equal; jödincu to join, unite. Kol. jodi pair. Pa. jorto join, mix together. Kui jõſe pair. Kur. joſā id.; jõộnā to unite or join to, put into shape. Malt. jóra pair; jóſare to be united, copulate; joratre, jórye to unite, couple. Br. joſa pair, match; jõſa kanning to put in. (H. jor union, pair; joſi pair, equal; jornā to join, unite, tie, collect, etc. Mar. jodnē id.; jod, joļi pair, etc. Turner, S. vv. jor?, jornu, jurnu.

Ta. cöti (-pp-, -tt-) to search, investigate, examine, test, cleanse. Ma. sõdhikka, cödikka, cötikka to search, question. Ko. co.dc- (co'dc-) to examine, test. Ka. sõdisu to search, examine. Kod. co dïi n. taste; co'dï no‘t- to taste (no:ț- to look at). Tu. śödhipuni, śõdhiyuni, sodiyuni to search, examine, try, assay. Te, sõdincu to search, examine; ? sõdi, sõde fortune-telling by a gypsy woman. /Skt. śudh-, caus. śodhay- to put to test, try, examine.

Ta. coli business, concern, affair, difficulty. Ma. cõli harrassing business; jõli trouble. Ko. jo lyv affair, news. To. swï·ly busi- Ka. jõli, jõļi concern, business, affair. Te. jõli concern, business, affair. /? < IA. ness, Z

Ta. ñāyam, nāyam, niyāyam justice, law, argument, debate, usage. Ma. ñāyam reason, right, complaint, custom. Ko. na‘ym (obl. na'yt-) justice, decision, dispute; na'ymgaörn headman. To. no'ym (obl. no'yt-) dispute, the tribal council. Ka. nyāya, nāya, nėya right, justice, argument, dispute, quarrel, lawsuit, judgment. Koș. ne ya”, (in song) ña'ya" dispute. Tu, nyāya, nāya justice, law, quarrel; right, just. Te. nyāyamu, nāyamu, nėyamu method, justice; just. Skt. nyāyamethod, fitness, lawsuit, judgment, argument. Pa. ñāya- id. Pkt. ņāya-, nāya- id. D

Ka. dilla, dilla unnerved, tottering state, agitation of mind, fear; șillisu to totter, become agitated. Tu. dily, ļīla, dīlu loose, unrestrained. Te. Pillamu stupefaction, weariness, weakness; dilla-padu DICTIONARY 37 to be astounded, stupefied, unnerved, be wearied; dīlu loose, lean, thin, weak; to become loose; dilā weakness; weak; dīlu weariness, thinness, looseness; wearied, weak; to grow tired or weak. /Mar. Ņhilā loose, slack; dhillī slackness; dhīl id.; loose, slack. H. dhīlā loose, weak. Turner, s.v. Ņhilo: Pkt. Ņhilla-, connection improbable with Pkt. sadhila-, sidhila- (cf. entry 133, Ka. sadal(u)); contra Pischel $150.

Te. dokka hard covering of a nut, etc., shell. Pa. (S) doki tortoise shell. Go. (Koya) dok shell (of tortoise, egg). Kui ļāki skull, shell (of tortoise, turtle, coconut, egg). /Mar. doki, dokē the head. Turner, s.v. doko. T, D

Ta. takku dodge, trick. Ka. takk, bikki fraud, dishonest doings. Te. takku to pretend, feign; n. pretending, pretense. Mar. thakņē to be deceived; thak, ţhag a knave, rogue. Turner, s.v. țhag, țhagnu.

Ta. tanțam staff, stick, branch of tree, club, pestle, punishment, penalty, loss, army; tanțu staff, stick, branch tree, club, pestle, bridge of nose, army; tanți (-pp-, -tt-) to punish. Ma. tanțu stick, staff, pole for bearing a burden, oar; daņdam stick, staff, punishment, army; dandikka to punish. Ko. taņd handle of broom, bridge of nose; tadm (obl. tadt-) a fine; dand punishment, fine; fight, marauding; daņạm (obl. dandt-) loss; dandc- (dandc-) to punish. To, todm fine paid to members of assembly belonging to opposite sub-caste, for contempt of assembly; tod army. Ka. tandu staff, club, heavy (iron) club; danda stick, staff, cudgel, oar, punishment, fine, army; dandisu to punish; danļu army. Koď. tanại big stick. Tu. dantè walking stick, staff; dandu oar; army; danda staff, stick, punishment, loss; daņdipuni, dandisuni to punish. Te. daņdamu rod, stick, staff, punishment, army, collection; dandincu to punish; dandu army, multitude; danļūdu Yama; danduga, danduva, daņduvu an extortion, fine, loss. / Skt. danda- stick, staff, club, sceptre as a symbol of power, violence, army, punishment, fine. Cf. also L. V. R. 1935. 64. Cf. also DED 2479, for items about which there is uncertainty whether they are borrowed from Skt. or are originally Dravidian.

Ta. tanțai trouble, vexation; tanță id., dispute, squabble. Ka. . tanțe quarrel, dispute, trouble, annoyance. Koď. tanțe trouble, annoy- Tu. tante id., meddling. Te. tanța, tanțā difficulty, trouble, dispute, slander. H. tāță, țățā wrangling, noisy quarrel. Mar. tātā ance. 38 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN worm. quarrel, a troublesome business. The Skt. root tand- to beat, which is compared by Kulkarni, is found in the Dhātupātha only.

Ta. tattu blotch, slight swelling as from the bite of an insect K Te.). Ka. taddu, daddu rash, herpes; ringworm. Tu. taddu an eruption or swelling, erysipelas; daddu ringworm, herpes. Te. daddu, dadduru herpes; a slight swelling of the skin, as from the bite of an insect. Pa. dad ringworm. Kui dado, dadu rough white patches on the skin that cause irritation and itching, dry itch. Kuwi (F) tadū ring- Kur. daddū id. /Skt. dadrŭ-, dardū cutaneous eruption, kind of leprosy. Pa. Pkt. daddu- id. H. dad ringworm, herpes, shingles. Turner, s.v. dād. Mayrhofer, s.v. dadrúh.

Ta. tapalai a kind of metal vessel; tavalai metallic pot with a wide mouth. Ma. tavala, takala a small cooking vessel of brass. Ko. tapa'l metal water-vessel. Ka. tapale, tappale, tapēli a round brass or copper cooking vessel. Tu. tapalè a large metallic cooking vessel, saucepan. Te. tapēla a small or portable vessel of any metal. Mar. tapelē, tapeli a culinary utensil (said to be a derivative of Skt. tap- to be hot); tavli a metal or earthen vessel.
Ta. tappaņam tacking needle. Ka. dabbana, dabbaļa pack-needle. Tu. dabbana bodkin, large packing needle. Te. dabbanamu id. Mar. dābhan pack-needle.

Ta. tampalam red spittle caused by chewing betel, refuse of chewed betel. Te, tamma, (K also) tammalamu chewed mass or lump of betel leaves and areca nuts. /Skt. tāmbūla- betel leaf. Pkt. tambolaid. H. tābol id. Turner, s. v. tamol.

Ta. tarukkam, tarkkam reasoning, arguing, discussion, dispute; tarukku disputation; takkam dispute, objection. dispute, objection. Ma. tarkam reasoning, dispute. Ka. tarka Ka. tarka id., discussion. Kod. takki talk, words; language. Tu. tarka dispute, discussion. Te. tarkamu reasoning, discussion. /Skt. tarka- reasoning, confutation. Pkt. takka id.

Ta. taruppai, tarppai the sacred grass, Poa cynosuroides. Ko. dab, da(b) pul grass, Andropogon schoenanthus. Ka. darbha, darbhe, darbe, dabbe P. cynosuroides. Tu. darbhè, darbe id. Te. darbha id. /Skt. darbha- bunch of grass. Pkt. dabbha id. (Eragrostis cynosuroides Beauv. - Poa cynosuroides Retz. A. s. is a different species.)

Ta. tavacam grain, esp. dry. Ko. davcm (obl. davct-) grain in general. Ka. tavasa, davasa corn, grain. Tu. davasa produce of the field, grain in general. Te. (B) davasamu grain. /Skt. yavasa- grass, fodder. Pkt. javasa- id.

Ta. talam thickness as of a board, heaviness. Ka. daļa thick- DICTIONARY 39 ness, stoutness, solidness. Tu. daļa thick, stout, robust. Te. daļamu id., much, great; thickness. Skt. drịha- firm, hard, strong, solid, massive; dşdham firmly, thoroughly, much. Pkt. dadha - Skt. drờha-. Turner, s. v. daro (esp. Sgh. daļa hard).

Ta. talam army. Ma. talam, dalam id.; daļavāyi a general. Ka. dara, daļa army; daravāyi a general. Kod. daļaba'y id. Tu. dala, daļavāda army; daļavāyi general of an army. Te. daļamu, daļamu army; daļavāyi general. /Skt. dala a detachment of troops. H. dal, Mar. dal army. Turner, s. v. dal.

Ko. talm (obl. talt-) palm of hand. Ka. tala, tala level surface; palm of the hand, sole of the foot; lower part, base, bottom (taļa is one of the tatsamas). Tu. tala, tala base, bottom. Te. talamu id., surface, palm of hand, sole of foot. Kuwi (F) talepau sole of foot. /Skt. talasurface, base, palm of hand, sole of foot.

Ta. tali temple, sacred shrine, place, room. Ma. taļi temple, holy building, asylum, assembly hall. Ka. tali fence, place of refuge, asylum, a covert, choultry for travellers, the building appointed for the distribution of food to brahmans, etc. /Skt. sthalī- place, spot. Pkt. thali- id.

Ta. talikai eating-plate, platter. Ma. talika metal plate turned up at the rim, plate to measure out boiled rice in temples. Ka. talige, tanige a metal plate turned up at the rim. Kod. talia plate. Te. taliga, taliya a dish for rice used in a Vaishnava temple. Skt. sthālavessel, plate, cup, bowl, pot; sthālī- earthen dish or pan, cooking vessel. BHS sthālaka-, sthālikā- pot. Pa. thālaka-, thālikā - id. Pkt. thalliāearthen dish. H. thaliyā plate, dish, platter. Cf. DED 2600.
Ta, tarai land, ground; tarai id., the earth. Ma. tara ground, mound, elevated ground. Skt. dharā- the earth.

Ta. tācari, tācan Vaišnava non-brahmin mendicant; tācari-ppāmpu hermit snake, large rock snake, as having an upright white streak like the forehead mark of a tācari. Ko. da'cn n. pr. bullock with white star on forehead; fem. da'c ( da c-y); da.cn man who begs from house to house; n. pr. man whose father begged thus to get the people's blessings when he had no son. Ka. dāsa, dāsara, dāsari servant; Vaishṇava religious mendicant; dāsa-hāvu, dāsara-hāvu, dāsari-hāvu boa (said to be called so because it has an upright white line on the forehead, or because marked with white streaks, like Vaishnavas). Te. dasari Vaishnava mendicant of the Sudra class; dāsari-pāmu a kind of snake. Skt. dāsaservant.

Ta. tāci, tāti maidservant; dancing girl, harlot. To, to Oy maid- 40 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN Ko. ta'ſ ness. servant. Ka. dāsi id.; harlot. Tu. dāsi maidservant. Te. dási id.; dancing girl. Kuwi (S) dáseni dancing girl. /Skt. dāsi- female servant, harlot.

Ta. tāți chin, beard, dewlap, hanging excrescence under a cock's neck; tāțai cheeks, chaps, jawbone; tāpjaws, adam's apple; tavațai cheek. Ma. tāți jawbone, chin, beard; tāța dewlap of a bull. (obl. ta't-) cheek just beside mouth. Ka. dāļi beard; dāde tusk, fang, jawbone; davaṣe jawbone. Kod. ta'ời beard; ta'ời kuțți, (Mercara) ta di kokki chin; davade chin; davade cheek. Tu, dādè tusk, fang; dāļi beard; davadè jaw, cheek. Te. davuda id. Go. tādwă chin. Skt. dāhā- tusk; dādhikabeard; tusk. Pkt. dadha- tusk; dādhia- beard, chin. H. dāșhā fang; dāșhi beard. Turner, s. v. dāro, dāri.

Ta. tățți cleverness, skill, bravery, fluency. Ma. dhāți bold- Ka. dăți, dhăți quickness in writing, fluency in reading, practice in a science, haste. Te. dhāți fluency, rapidity, vigor. Skt. dhārstyaboldness, violence. Pkt. *dhāțha-, *dhāțhia-, or the like (cf. dhattha-, dhițțha- bold).

Ta. tāmpāļam salver of a large size. Ka. tāmbāla, tāmbāņa a metal dish. Tu. tämbana a metallic dish or tray. Te. tāmbālamu tray, salver. Mar. tāmhan a circular metal dish; tãblē, tabli a small metal drinking vessel. (Both are said by Kulkarni to be < Skt. tāmracopper).

Ta. tarai blade of weapon, sharpness. Ma. dhāra edge of a sword or instrument. Ko. ta'r sharp edge (of weapon, tool, stone). Ka. dhāre sharp edge of a sword or any cutting instrument. Tu. dhāre sharpness. Te. dhāra sharpness or edge of any cutting instrument. Go. (A) dhar edge of knife. /Skt. dhārā- sharp edge, blade.

Ta, tāvaļam lodging, place of residence; tāvu resting-place, lodging, shelter. Ma. tāvaļam lodging place, retirement, . Ka. tāvu, ļāvu, thāvu place, abode. Te. tävalamu id., home; tāvu place, locality, abode, residence; thāvu place, house, residence. /Skt. sthāman- place. Pkt. thāma-, Apabhramsa țhāma- id. H. thăw id. Mar. thāv id. Turner, s. v. thāū.
Ta. tālam cymbal. Ma. tālam id. Ka. tāla, tāla, tāņa id. Kod. tāļa id. Tu. tāla, tāla Te. tālamu id. id. Skt. tāla- cymbal. BHS tāda- id. Pa. tāla- id.

Ta. tikku direction; protection, shelter, aid. Ma. dikku direction, region; refuge. Ko. dik protection, aid. To. tik id. Ka. dikku direction; refuge, protection, help. Kod. dikkö direction. Tu. dikku direction; refuge, protection. Te. dikku id. Skt. diś- (nom. sg. dik) direction, country. id. DICTIONARY 41

Ta. titti bellows, purse, leather bag, a kind of flute or pipe; tuti bellows; tutti bass-pipe. Ma. titti bagpipe. Ko. tiod bellows. Ka. titti, tidi leather bag, bag in general, pair of bellows. Tu. sidi, sidè bellows; tuti a sort of drone corresponding to a bagpipe. Te. titti leather bag or case, a skin, any bag-like thing, bellows or pair of bellows, bagpipe. Kuwi (F) tittū (pl. 'nga) bellows; (S) tithunga id., bagpipes. Skt. dệti- leather bag, a skin, bellows. Pkt. *diti-, *didi-, dii- id.

Ta. tiru, ciri, ci śri, Lakşmi, holiness, sacredness. Ko. tir im the Toda ti:- buffaloes; tir er buffalo calf at Toda calf sacrifice; ciry prosperity, happiness of life. To, ti: the most sacred grade of Toda dairy; ti: ir the buffaloes of the ti'-dairy (i.e. the holy buffaloes). Skt. śri- Lakşmi, holiness, sacredness. Pkt. siri- id.

Ta. tuti (-pp-, -tt-) to praise, flatter, worship; n. praise, eulogy, fame. Ka. tuti, stuti praise, eulogy, flattery; tutisu, stutisu, stutiyisu to praise, worship. Kod. tudi- (tudiv-, tudiñj-) to be praised; (tudio-, tudic-) to praise. Tu. tuti, stuti praise. Te, stuti id.; stutincu to praise. /Skt. stuti praise, adulation. Skt. st- normally becomes Ta. t-, but there may be a MIA intermediary with th-, and also -d-, viz. *thudi-; Pa. thuti-, Pkt. thuti-, thui- are the attested forms.
