Ta. turai chief, lord, master, ruler, gentleman, nobleman, European gentleman; turaicci, turaicāni lady, matron, mistress, European lady; turaittanam government. Ma. tura, dhvara master, lord, a man of rank. Ko. doyr European man; fem. dorca'ny. To. twary European (in songs). Ka. dore chief, king, master, a man of the ruling class; doresāni lady, mistress; doretana kingship, royalty, the rank or function of a king, government, rule. Kod. dore king, European. Tu. doré, dhore master, lord, king, ruler. Te. dora a chief, lord, ruler, governor, master, owner, an equal; doratanamu government, dominion, rule, reign, sovereignty. Pa. dora rich man, merchant, moneylender. Kuwi (S) doreesi gentleman. Skt. dhurya- leader, chief > dhaureya- superior > Pa. dhoreyya- (see Edgerton, BHS Dict., s.v. dhaura-), Pkt. dhoreya- (and dhojja-) id.

Ta. tulai steelyard, weight, well-sweep; tula id., balance, single shaft of a cart; tulām balance, steelyard, well-sweep, main beam in roof; tūlam beam of a house. Ma. tula balance; tulām id., beam, joist, sloping beam in a roof, well-sweep. Ko. tol log used in breaking bullocks to plow. Ka, tula, tule, tulā, tole balance, scales, weight, beams in roof of a house; dūla a beam of timber. Tu. tolè, tulè beam, log. Te. dūlamu beam. Kui tūli ridge of a house. /Skt. tula- bal- 42 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN ance, weight, a kind of beam in the roof of a house.

Ta. tunnu (tunni-) to sew, stitch; tunnam sewing, needlework; tunnal sewing; tunnar tailors, cobblers. Ma, tunnuka to sew, stitch; tunnal sewing; tunnikka to get clothes made. Kur, tunnā to plait or repair baskets, mats, etc., (Hahn) mend, repair. Malt. tunye to sew. /NIA *tun to mend, darn. Turner, S. v. tunnu.
Ta. tūcu cloth, garment, cotton; tūcar washermen. Ka. dūsu, dūsa, dūşya cloth, cotton, calico. Skt. dūşya- a tent. . BHS důşyacloth, cotton. Pa. dussa- cloth, clothes. Pkt. dūsa- id.

Ta. tēti, teyti date, day of the month; titi lunar day. Ma. tiyyati, tiyati, tēti day of the month, date. Ko. te dy id. Ka, titi, tithi lunar day. Tu. tēdi a day of the solar month; tithi a lunar day. Te. tēdi a date, day of the month; tithi lunar day. Skt. tithi - lunar day.

Ta. tēvatāci, tēv-ațicci, tēv-ațiyāl temple dancing girl, prostitute. Ma. tēvațiyāļ id.; (vulg.) tēvițiyā- makan bastard. Ko. te vry prostitute; te vry mog son of a whore. /Skt. devadāsī- temple dancing girl (ațicci and ațiyāļ are calques on dāsī).

Ta. tēvu, tēvan god; tēvar deities; teyvam, taivam god. Ma. tēvan a deity. Ko. devr god. To, töw id. Ka. dēva id.; devva, devvu demon, evil spirit. Kod. de va god. Tu. dēva id.; daiva deity, god; devva demon, evil spirit. Te. dēva god; dēvara id., master; daivamu god. /Skt. deva- god; daiva-, daivya- divine. Pkt. devagod; devva divine.

Ta. tõņi boat, dhoney, ship, float, raft, canoe, water-trough. Ma. toņi trough, bathing tub, boat. Ka, dāņi, dāņi id. Tu, dāņi Tu. dõņi boat. Te. done a large boat, a small vessel or ship, (B also) a trough. Skt. droņi- wooden trough or tub, any vessel or implement made of wood. Pa. Pkt. doni- id., canoe. H. Joni small boat. Mar. doni Turner, s.v. duno, dunu. canoe. N id.

Ta. nakai jewels. Ma. naka jewel. To. naxy Ka. naga an ornament, an article, a piece, a load of articles, a bullock load. Kod. naga jewelry. Tu. naga jewels, ornaments; goods, property. Te, naga a jewel or ornament, a metal vessel, a bullock load of tobacco, etc. /Skt. naga- mountain. id., rock, precious stone, jewel. Mar. nag id., an article or item (as of implements, pieces of apparel, etc., in enumerating them), a piece. H. nag DICTIONARY 43

Ta. nankặram anchor. Ma. nankūram id. Ka. nangal, langar id. Tu. nangarų, nangalų, langarų id. Te. langaru id. Skt. nāgaraanchor (Tilakamañjarī, pp. 119, 122, etc.). Mar. nãgar id. H. langar id. ( Pers. langar). All ultimately < Greek öykūpa.

Ta. nattu nose-ornament. Ka. nattu id. Tu. nattų, nattu, nartu id. Te. nattu ring worn by women on the side of the nose. Go. (Muria) nath nosering. Skt. nastā hole bored through the septum of the nose; nastaka- septum of the nose (of cattle) or hole bored in it. Pkt. ḥatthānose-rope. H. nath nose-rope, a ring worn in the nose by women.

Ta. nāți pulse, artery, vein, tendon, ligament; nāri tubularity, tube, a measure of capacity (= 8 ollocks), Indian hour (= 24 minutes), weaver's shuttle, quiver, the 25th nakșatra; nārikai Indian hour. Ma. nāți, nāļi any tubular organ, vein, artery, the pulse; nāri tube, bamboo joint, a measure (of fluids); närikai an Indian hour. Ko, na ty pulse in wrist, sexual potency; na fy heart-beat, pulse. To. no ty pulse in wrist. Ka. nāļi any tubular organ of the body, as artery, vein, nerve, etc., the pulse; nāri Indian hour; nāļi tube, water channel, weaver's shuttle; lāļi weaver's shuttle. Tu. nāļi the pulse, a blood-vessel, artery, or vein; lali a weaver's shuttle. Te. nāļi any tubular organ of the body, artery, vein, the pulse. Skt. nāļi- any tubular organ (as a vein or artery of the body), pipe, tube, the pulse. Turner, s. vv. näril, nalil.

Ta. nāņayam stamped coin; uprightness, honesty, probity, honor as in money-dealings, punctuality, extraordinary facts or supposed facts in nature as of the cobra shrinking from the nāka-tāļi root, supposed virtue or action of a plant as the presenting of a herb to the eyes as a cure of ophthalmia, restriction, rule, that which is of good quality as a commodity; nāņakam stamped coin. Ma. nāņiyam, nāṇyam honesty, credit, what is current as reports, proverbs, coin, esp. gold coin. Ka. nāṇya fineness, goodness, good quality as that of grain, cloth, character, etc., honesty, truth, a coin, money, small pieces of silver money. Tu. nāṇya money, coin. Te. nāņemu a coin; honesty, trustworthiness; nãạemu quality, fineness, ascertaining the quality or fineness of anything, character, honesty; a coin; adj. fine, good, honest. /Skt. nāņakacoin or anything stamped with an impression. Pkt. ņāņaka-, ņāņaga- id.

Ta. nāyar a caste of Hindus in Malabar. Ma. nāyan, nāyar the Sūdras of Kēraļa; soldiers of all castes. Koờna'yammë a Nāyar man; fem. na'yarci. Tu. nāyare, näyimāre a Nāyar of Malabar. Skt. nāyaleader, chief.

Ta. nicam own; certainty, assurance, ascertainment, truth, veracity; nicavān true, sincere, upright, honest man. Ma. nijam own; cer- 44 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN tainty. Ka. nija innate, own; real, true, actual, genuine, real state or shape, reality, truth. Tu. nija own; truth, veracity, certainty, reality; true, certain, sure, real. Te. nijamu own; truth, reality, fact, truthfulness, veracity, certainty; true, real, actual, certain, positive; nija-padu to be verified, proved real or true; nija-paracu to realize; prove, establish; nijamari a truthful man; nijamugă truly, really, actually; nijāyati (coll.) truthfulness, honesty, uprightness. Kuwi (S) nizomi (z j) truth. /Skt. nija- innate, own.

Ta. nimpam margosa. Ma. nimpam Melia azadirachta. Ka. nimba Azadirachta indica Juss. Te. nimbamu id., neem or margosa tree. Pa. līm id. Go. (Muria) nimbu, (A) lim id. Kui lima the nim tree. Skt. nimba- Azadirachta indica. [M. azadirachta Linn. - A. indica Adr.)

Ka. nimbi, nimbe, limbe the acid lime, Citrus medica. Tu. nimbe, limbi, limbe the lemon fruit, C. bergamia. Te. nimma the lime tree. Kol. nimba lime, lemon; (SR) limbū lemon. Ga. (S) nimbe lime tree. Kui lembu lemon, lime. Kuwi (F) limba lemon; (S) limma lime, lemon. Skt. nimbū(ka)- the common lime, C. acida. Turner, s. v. nibu. Mayrhofer, s. v. nimbū-. C. medica Linn.; var. 1 medica proper (the citron); var. 2 limonum (the lemon); var. 3 acida (the sour lime of India); var. 4 limetta (the sweet lime of India). C. aurantium Linn.; var. 1 aurantium proper (the sweet orange); var. 2 bigaradia (the bitter or Seville orange); var. 3 bergamia (the bergamotte orange). ]

Ka, nepa, neva, nevana, nevanu pretence, pretext, plea. Kod. neva"na pretence. Tu. nevana pretence, pretext, trick. Te. nepamu, nevamu id.; blame, imputation, charge, accusation. Skt. nibhasembling; (at end of bahuvrīhi cpds.) appearance, pretext. BHS, Pa. nibhāappearance, sheen. Pkt. ņihă- deceit; ņivva- pretence (DNM). Nepali ni(h)ũ excuse, pretence (see Turner).

Ta. nēmi (-pp-, -tt-), niyami (-pp-, -tt-) to appoint; nēmam appointment. Ma. niyamikka to order, appoint; nēmam rule, service of a raja. Ko. ne'mc- (ne.mc-) to select, appoint. Ka. nēma, niyama appointment; nēmisu, niyamisu to appoint. Tu. nēmaka appointment; determination, choice; nēmisuni to appoint, determine. Te. nēmincu, niyamincu to determine, fix, appoint, commission; nēmamu, (K also) nimamu rule, religious regulation. Go. nēmānā to obey instructions regarding diet in illness; (Ph.) nemanā to observe vows. /Skt. niyamarule, regulation; agreement, arrangement; etc. H. niyam, nem reid. DICTIONARY 45 P, B ace. . near.

Ta. pakațai ace upon dice. Ma. pakața, pakița id. Ka. pagade a mark on a die, a die or piece for playing backgammon, the play itself. Kod. pagade chess. Tu. pagade Te. pagada id. Mar. pagdā a draught (in the game). Connected with Mar. pag square on a chessboard, etc., which is undoubtedly the same as pag foot; on the very uncertain origin of this, Turner, s. v. pagdandi.

Ta. pakkam side, nearness; pakkal side, one's class or tribe. Ma. pakkam, pakkal, pakku side. Ko. pak, in phrases: tan paka'ſ by himself, of his own accord, tam paka'ſ with one another, etc. To. pak side. Ka. pakka, pakke, pakku id., proximity. Kod. pakka Tu. pakke side. Te. pakka side; near, adjacent; pakkiya side; ? prakka side, part, direction. Ga. (oll.) paki side. Skt. paksa- wing, side, proximity. Pkt. pakkha- id. Turner, s. v. pākho. b Ta. pakși, pațci, pakki bird. Ma. pakși, pakki id. Ko. paky id. Ka. pakși, pakki, hakki id. Kod. pakši, pakki id.; penis of immature boy. Tu. pakki bird. Te. pakși, pakki id. Ko. paksiak male bird; paksin female bird ( Mar.; tatsama from Skt.). Skt. pakşinbird. Pa, pakkhin- id. Pkt. pakkhi- id.

Ta. pankāru, pankāram, vankāram gold. Ko. banga'ry jewels, gold or silver chain. Ka. bangāra, vangāra gold; ongāra id., gold ornaments. Tu. bangārų, bangāra gold. Te. bangāru, bangăramu, bangaruvu id. Kol. (SR) bangār id. Konda baŋaram id. Kuwi (F) bangara, (S) bangăra id. /Skt. bhạngāra- gold pitcher or vase; gold (lex.).
Ta. pankuni month Phalguni (February March). Ma. pankuni id. Skt. phālguna- the month of the phalguni asterism. Pa. Pkt. phagguņa-

Ta. paccavațam, paccatam a long piece of cloth used as a blanket, bedsheet, or screen. Ma. paccavațam an entire piece of cloth (32 cubits); blanket. Ko. paca'd (obl. paca't-), paca'd vara'ſ cloak sewed together from two lengths. Ka. paccavaļa, paccada a stout cotton cloth (24 cubits long and 2 cubits broad), used as a wrapper or cover at night. Kod. paccada white cloth for saris. Tu. paccade shawl. Te. paccadamu bed sheet, cloak. /Skt. pracchada a cover, wrapper, blanket. Pkt. pacchaa- garment, sheet. Cf. entry 241 for vațam, etc. < Skt. pața-.
Ka. pañju torch. Tu. pañji, pañju id. Te. panju, panjāyā id. H. panji a sort of torch with five branches for lights (< Pers.).

To. poz ( cloak (only in stories). Ka. pañce, pañjā, pañje a small dötra used for various purposes. Kod. pañce waist-cloth. Te. 46 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN pance a man's lower garment. /Mar. pañcā a short dhoti ( Pers.).
Ta. pațanku standard, large banner. Ma. patannu flag. Te. . padaga id., banner. Skt. patākā-, pațākā- flag, banner. BHS pațākāid. Pa. patākā-, pațāka- id. Pkt. padāga-, padãā- id.

Ta. pațam cloth for wear, painted or printed cloth, picture, upper garment; pațām cloth. Ma. pațam fine cloth, sheet, chequered cloth, picture. To. padm (obl. padt-) picture, photograph. Ka. pața, pada, padu cloth, chequered cloth, picture. Kod. pața picture. Tu. padambu a rough canvas cloth. Te. pațamu cloth, garment, picture. b Ta. pațțu silk cloth, silk yarn, sackcloth of Indian hemp; pațți cloth, puttee, bandage. Ma. pațțu silk, sackcloth made of hemp. Ko. patrag. To. poțy clothes. Ka. pațțu, pațța cloth, woven silk; patte, pațți silk . Kod. patti silk cloth. Tu. pațțè silk, piece of cloth, tape; pațți strip of cloth. Te. pațța, pațțā sackcloth; pațțamu silk thread; pațțu silk; patte tape. Skt. pața- cloth, garment, painted cloth, picture; pați- a kind of cloth; pațța- cloth, colored or fine cloth, woven silk. Turner, s.v. pāta.

Ta. pațāy vain pomp, bragging. Ko. bara'y haughtiness; bara'yga'rn haughty man. Ka. baļāyi vain pomp, bragging. Kod. bada'yi pride, self-conceit. Tu. baļāyi, pațāvu, pattanna, pațțanga boasting, bragging. Te. badāyi id., egotism, pride. H. barhāi increase, aggrandizement. Turner, s. vv. barāĩ(Nepali and some other languages have meaning 'boast') and baſāunu.

Ta. pați (-pp-, -tt-) to learn, study, read, recite, chant, say, tell, praise; pațippi (-pp-, -tt-) to teach; pațippu learning, study, reading, chanting, instruction. Ma. pațikka to learn, read, teach; pațittam, pațippu learning; pațippikka to teach. education. Ka. pațhisu, pathiyisu to read or repeat aloud, recite, study, express. Kod. paļi- (padip-, padic-) to learn. Tu. padipuni id. Te. pațhincu to read, recite. Kur. paſhnā to read, recite formulas. Malt. parye to read. /Skt. path- to read, study, learn, recite. Pkt. padh- id. H. paſhnā id. Turner, s. v. parnu.
Ta. pațikkam, pațiyakam spittoon, pot for receiving water used for an idol. Ma. pațikkam spittoon. Ka. padiga id. Tu. padlậlya id. Te. paạiga id. /Skt. pratigraha- spittoon. Pkt. padiggaha- id.

Ta. pațikkāram, pațuki alum. Ma. pațikkāram, pațikakkāram id. Ka. pațigăra, pataka, patika, patike id. Tu. pațikära id. Te. paţikāramu, patika, pațiki id. /Skt. sphaţikā-, sphaţikārð- alum. Turner, s.v. phaſkiri.

Ta. pațu clever skillful person, sound intellect. Ma. patu clever, Ko. paryp DICTIONARY 47 a smart. Ko. bat feat, clever deed; batga:rn clever man, winner. To. potxo'rn clever person. Ka. pašu clever, skillful. Tu. pațy id. Te. pațuvu id. /Skt. pațu- clever, skillful, cunning.

Ta. pațțam plate of gold worn on forehead as an ornament or badge of distinction, title of office or dignity, regency, reign. Ma. pattam ornament of the forehead, diadem, high dignity, ordination and tonsure. Ko. pațm (obl. pațt-) diadem, title. To. pot crown; poțm (obl. poţt-) throne, title, power, ability. Ka. pațța frontlet with a golden tablet with which king is decorated at coronation, royalty, royal throne, dignity, office. Kod. patta inauguration as king. Tu. pațţa crowning, ordination, throne, rank. Te. pațţamu coronation, frontlet, tiara, diadem, a title; pațți frontlet. Skt. pațța- frontlet, tiara, diadem.

Ta. pattayam, pațțaiyam, pațțā, pațțā-kkatti sword; pațțam id., weapon; pațțicam weapon. . Ma. pațțayam broad sword; pațțasam, pațțiśam sharp-edged spear, Ka. pattaya, pațe, pattā a long and broad sword; pațțiśa, pațțisa spear with a sharp edge. Te. pațţă-katti double-edged sword; pattiyamu, pațțemu sword; pațțisamu a sort of weapon. /Skt. pațțiśa- spear with a sharp edge or some other weapon with three points. H. pață a long, broad sword with two edges; a wooden foil; patti a foil. Cf. Skt. pattra(ka)- blade of sword or knife, knife, dagger.

Ta. pațțan brahman priest of a temple. Ma. pațțan a class of foreign brahmans, often traders. Ka. bhatta, batta, bața a learned brah- Kod. paštë brahman; fem. pațțati; adj. paſta. Tu. bhatte, batte priest, soothsayer. Te. bhațțūdu title affixed to the names of learned brahmans. Skt. bhatta- lord; part of the name of a learned brahman.

Ko. baty pile of wood covered with earth by which charcoal is made. Ka. bațți kiln, furnace, still. Tu. batti id. Te. batti a still. /Skt. bhrăştra- gridiron. Pkt. bhattha- id. H. bhatt(h)i distillery, furnace, kiln.

Ta. paņam wealth, coin, money, sp. coin (fanam) of varying local values. Ma. panam coin, fanam, money; paņa-ttūkkam weight of a gold fanam. Ko. paņm (obl. pant-) money; four-anna piece. Ka. pana a small coin of silver or gold (fanam), wealth. Kod. paņa money. Tu, paņăvu 1/4 rupee, money, wealth; paņa-tūka the weight of a gold fanam. Te. paņamu a certain copper coin or its weight, wealth. Skt. pana a weight of copper used as a coin.
Ta. paņțāram religious mendicant, Saiva monk. Ma. pantāram Shaiva mendicant. Te. paņdāram n. of a certain caste. /Skt. piņdārareligious mendicant. man. 48 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN S.V.

Ko. baty cigar. To. paty id. Ka. batti id. Tu. batti id. /Skt. vart- anything rolled or wrapped round; dhūpa-varti-, dhumavarti a kind of cigarette. Cf. H. batti ( Skt. vart-), but not in this meaning.

Ta. panti row, series, line of persons seated for dining; stable for horses or elephants. Ma. panti row, esp. of feast-guests; range of buildings, stable; arrangement, order, Ko. pandy row of leaves with food at dry-funeral feast. Ka. panti, pante, panni row, series, row of people sitting down at a meal. Tu. pantè id. Te. banti a row, line, rank. Skt. pańkti- row, series, company (e.g. of persons eating together or belonging to the same caste). Pa. Pkt. panti- id. Turner, pãti.

Ta. paravā care, concern, harm. Ma. parava concern, care. Ko. parva:dy ila', parva'y ila: it doesn't matter, it is a little good, it's all right. Ka. paravā, parave, parvā care, concern about, regard, heed, anxiety; paravā illa it is of no consequence, never mind. Kod. paruva ille it doesn't matter. Tu. parava, parva concern, care, regard, respect. Te. parvā regard, respect, care for; parvā lēdu never mind, no matter. Br. parvā care, concern ( Pers.). / H. parwă care, concern, anxiety (< Pers.).

Ta. parāmari (-pp-, -tt-) to examine, consider; take care of, maintain, support, cherish, conduct (as an office), discharge (as duties); parāmarippu maintenance, support, management; parāmarici (-pp-, -tt-) to consider. Ma. parāmarsikka to consider; take care of. Ko. para'vary a cure, cured. Ka. parāmarśisu, parāmarisu, parāmbarisu, parāmmarisu to examine, be considerate; treat or attend kindly, tend or take care of, console. Tu. parāmbaripuni to consider; take care of, nurse; parāmbarikè investigation; care, protection. Te. parāmarsincu, parāmarisincu to examine, inquire after; condole with, console; parāmarśamu, parāmarika, parāmarisa examination, inquiry; attentions, care, condolence. /Skt. parāmṛść to lay hold of, touch, consider, deliberate. BHS parāmrs- (see Edgerton, BHS Dict. for meanings). Pa. parāmas- to touch, hold on to, deal with, be attached to or fall a victim to. Pkt. parāmaristo consider, touch (so Sheth).

Ta. parvam, paruvam knot, joint, the five religious ceremonial days in each fortnight, festival. Ma. parvvam, paruvam knot, joint, period, festival. Ko. pabm festival in February-March (Kota Texts, text 41); parv feast given in payment of vow, to avert ill consequences of transgression, or on being readmitted to caste. To. parf feast given by Badagas once a year to which Todas go. Ka. parva, parba festival, DICTIONARY 49 holiday. Tu. parba, pabba , id. . Te. pabbamu feast. Ga. (S) parrūb (pl. parbūl) festival. Kur. parab, parbī festival, feast. Malt. parbe festival. /Skt. parvan- knot, joint, the days of the changes of the moon, sacrifice (or festival] at a change of the moon, festival. Pkt. pavvaid. H. parb, parab id.

Ta. palakai plank, board; long shield. Ma. palaka plank, board; seat, footstool; shield. Ko. palg, pal plank; bench in main room of house. Ka. palage, palige, parige plank, board; shield. Kod. paleya wooden stool. Tu. palăyi plank, board. Te. palaka plank; bench. ? Pa. pakki stool. Br. palk plank. Skt. phalaka- board, wooden bench, shield. Pkt. phala(g)a-, phalaha- id. Turner, s.v. phaliyo.

Ta. paļinku crystal, crystal quartz, mirror. Ma. palunku crystal, glass. Ka. paļuku, palaku, paliku, palika crystal. Te. (B) palugu rock crystal. /Pa. phaļika- crystal. Pkt. phaliha- id. Pkt. phaliha- id. Sgh. paļiňgu id. (Skt. Sphatika-; Master, BSOAS 11.297 ff.).
Ta. pākār fort wall. Ka. pāgal, pāgala, păgăra encircling wall, rampart. Tu. pāgăra inclosure, fence, rampart. Skt. prākāra- wall, rampart. Pa. pakāra- id. Pkt. pāgāra-, pāāra- id.
Ta. pāku treacle, molasses, coarse sugar, palm sugar; any liquid food. Te. pāgu, pākamu, (K also) paku melted sugar, syrup, candy. /H. pāg syrup. Skt. pāka- is origin of Te, pākamu.
Ta. påkutam gift, present, royal revenue, tribute. Ka. pāvuda, pävada, pāguda a present. /Skt. prābhịta- gift. Pkt. pāhuộa- id.
Ta. pāccikai dice. Ma. pāccika id. Ka. pācike id. Te. pācika, pasika id. /Skt. pāśa(ka)- die. Turner, s.v. päso*. Mayrhofer, s.v. pāśakaḥ.

Ta. pāțakam anklet worn by women. Ma. pāțakam id. Ka. pädaga anklet worn by children and women. Tu. pādaga, pāduga anklet. Te. pādagamu silver anklet. Skt. pädakațaka- anklet. Pkt. *pāaadaga- > Dr. pādaga- (Godavarma, p. 205, gives a Pkt. pāagaďaga- (not found in the dictionaries] as the source; even though this might be expected, it is only *pāaadaga- that will contract to pädaga-).

Ta. påțai Indian pareira. Ma. pāța Cissampelus or Clypea. Ka. pädāvaļi-balli Clypea burmanni. /Skt. pāțhā- Clypea hernandifolia. Pkt. pādhā- id. (Prob. all the same species, but there has been considerable disagreement in the botanical terminology.)

Ta. pāțțiyami day after the full or new moon ( Te.). Ka. padya, pădiya, päţiva first day of a lunar fortnight. Tu. pädya id. Te. padyami id. /Skt. pratipad-, pratipada- first day of a lunar fortnight. Pkt. padivaā- id. H. pașiwā, pariwā id. Turner, s.v. parewa?. 50 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO- ARYAN

Ta. pāpam, pāvam sin, crime; an exclamation of pity. Ma. pāpam evil, sin; interj. alas! what a pity! Ko. pa pm (obl. pa'pt-) sin, injury; an exclamation of pity. Ka. pāpa sin, guilt; O misery! Kod. pa pa an exclamation of pity. Te. pāpamu sin, crime; alas! what a pity! / Skt. pāpa- sin, evil. L. V. R. 1935. 66.
Ma. pāļi tip of the ear. Ka. pāle, hāle, halle lobe of the ear. Tu. pāļi, pāļè tip of the ear. /Skt. pāli- lobe of the ear. Mar. pal outer curving edge of ear.
Ta. pāval wooden sandals. Ka. pāvuge, hāvuge, avuge, hävige, ävige shoe. Te. pāva (pl. pāvalu) a sandal. /Skt. pādukā- shoe. Pkt. pāuā- id.

Ta. pittu millet flour. To. it flour. Ka. pițțu, pițțe, hittu id., meal, powder. Tu. itļy flour. Te. pişța mu id., meal. Skt. pişța- crushed, ground; flour, meal. Pa. Pkt. pittha- id. Turner, s. v. pițho. b Ta. pittu, puțțu a kind of confectionery; piţtam dough. Ma. pittu, puttu a thin meal-cake, rice-bread. Ko. pițrice, ragi, etc, cooked so as to form a solid mass; food. To. it lump of boiled food other than rice; prț fried cake. Ka. pittu, pitte, hittu porridge (esp. of rāgi), food; puțțu salted dough baked. Kod. puțții a preparation of rice, wheat, or other grain. Tu. hitty porridge. Te. pittu flour boiled in steam. Skt. pișța- kneaded; cake, pastry; pișțaka- cake or anything made of flour (lex.). BHS pişțaka- cake. Turner, s. v. pițho.

Ta. pittaļai brass. Ma. pittaļa, piccaļa id. Ka. pittala, hittăți, hittăle id. Tu. pittalè id. Te. pittaļamu, pittalamu, ittadi, ittaļi id. Kol. pitol, (Hislop) pital id. Kui pitalo id. Kuwi (F) pītara, (s) pittada Kur. pitali, pitali id. Malt. piteli id. /Skt. pittala-, pitala- brass, bell-metal. Pkt. pittala- id. H. pītal id. Mar. pita! id. Turner, s. v. pital.

Ta. pirațai, piruțai plug of a lute, screw-nut. Ka. birade, birade peg or screw to tighten the strings of musical instruments; a cork. Te. biradă a cork, stopper, plug, peg. Mar. birdē a button and/or loop. Turner, s.v. biro, birko, for some items that may be connected.
Ta. pirukkam kidney. Ko. viky id. To. pïşk id. Br. bik kidney (Bray: borrowing from Jațki buk, Si. bukī). Skt. vřkka- kidney. Pa. Vakka id. NIA in general has forms with -u-; Turner, s.v. boknu.
Ta. puttam buttocks; pudendum muliebre; puțți waist. To. pïty buttocks. Skt. prstha- back. Pkt. puţtha- id. H. puţthā buttock. Turner, s.v. pith.

Ta. pūci (-pp-, -tt-) to perform acts of ceremonial worship; id. DICTIONARY 51 worpūcai worship. . Ma. pūjikka to honor, worship; pūja worship. To. pu'z- (pu'j-) to do worship at temple. Ka. pūjisu to worship; pūje worship. Kod. pu'j- (pu'ji-) to do the acts of worship. Tu. pūjè ship. Te. pūjincu to worship. Skt. pūj- to honor, worship; pūjāworship.

Ta. pūri (-pp-, -tt-) to be full, become perfect, thrive, abound; fill (tr.); puri (-pp-, -tt-) to fill up (tr.), inlay; purai (-pp-, -tt-) to be great; n. greatness, height, eminence. Ma. pūrikka to fill, accomplish; be full. To. pūry- (pürs-) to become full; pürc- (pürč-) to fill (tr.). Ka. pūray(i)su, pūravisu, pūrisu to fill, fill up, complete, fulfil; be filled, be completed, finished, be accomplished; pura, puru much, many, abundant. Tu. puresuni, pũraisuni to complete, fulfil, be satisfied, afford. Te. pūragincu to fulfil, accomplish; pūrincu to fill (tr.). Pa. pūr- to be completed. Kui pūri full; pūri āva to be full; pūri giva to fill; prusu full, filled; prusu inba to be full, filled; prusna fully. Ta. munțam head, forehead, clean-shaven head, bald head, skull; headless trunk, limbless body, undeveloped foetus, naked body, useless person, blockhead, globe, sphere, stump, stake; munțan shaven-headed a DICTIONARY 55 person, Śiva as having a skull in the hand; barber; muntanam shaving of the head; munți person with clean-shaven head; barber; munțitam shaving the head clean; munțai widow as having a shaven head. Ta. mutta-kkācu, muttai straight sedge, Cyperus rotundus; straight sedge tuber, C. pertenuis; mucalai, muyalai fragrant tuber of C. rotundus. Ta. mūcai crucible, earthen mould for casting molten metal. Ma. müsa id. Ka. musi, mūsi, mūse, mūşeid. Tu. mūsè, mūşè id. Te. mūsa, mūşa id. /Skt. mūşa- crucible.

Ta. vāņam arrow; rocket, fireworks, fire. Ma. vānam arrow; rocket. Ka. bāņa id. Kod. baina Tu. bāņa id.; rocket. Te. bāņamu id. Skt. bāņa-, vāņa- arrow. H. ban id., rocket.
Ta, vāttu duck, goose. Ma. båttu id. Ko, va't goose. Ka. bātu, båte duck. Kod. ba ti id. Tu. battu id., gander. /H. bat, batak, batak duck (< Pers.).
Ta. Vāram days of the week, a week. Ma. vāram a week-day. Ko, va'rm (va.rt-) a week. Ka. vāra day of the week. Tu vāra a week. Te. vāramu id. /Skt. vāra- day of the week.
Ka. bidiya shame, bashfulness. Tu. biļè id. Te. bidiyamu, bidemu id. Skt. vrid- to feel shame, be bashful. Pkt. vĩờia- ashamed.

Ma. vinta a copper pot for treasure. Ka. bindige a kind of metal water-vessel. Kod. bindige water-pot (for carrying). Tu. binde a small earthen pot. Te. bindiya, binde a metal pot. /Mar. bingā small metal vessel.

Ta. pilimpi, ? vilimpi bilimbi tree. Ma. vilimpi, vilumpi Averrhoa bilimbi. Ka. bilimbi id. Tu. bimbali, bimbili, bimbuli id. Te. bilibili id. From Malay belimbing, acc. to Ta. Lex. Hooker: 'native country unknown'; both A. carambola and A. bilimbi are probably 'natives of the New World, in which alone is a native species found; very likely . . . introduced by the Portuguese into India.'

Ta. villai that which is circular, scented tablet, patch, a kind of ear-ornament (villai-muruku), metal badge on a peon's belt, a kind of id., DICTIONARY 61 any tablet head ornament, ball of cooked rice available in temples (villai-ccättam); pillai that which is round as a patch of sandal paste, a tablet or tabloid, nut of a screw, badge of a peon, square tile, a head ornament. Ma. villa a metal plate, a badge of peons. Ka. bille a circular object, a round plate of metal, etc., the breastplate of a belt as of a peon. Kod. bille gold plate worn by woman at back of head. Tu. billè anything made in a flat form as a tablet or lozenge, a peon's badge, etc., a pane, panel. Te. billa, billa a dish, a cake as of soap, etc., a small tablet or tabloid, a brass or silver plate used as a peon's badge, a round cushion or pillow, a bit or piece of silver or gold tied to the waist-thread of a female infant. Kuwi (F) bīla wheel; (S) billa button, wheel. H. billā or flat piece of metal, badge worn by peons.

Ta. veņķai, vaņțai okra, Hibiscus esculentus; esculent okra, Abelmoschus esculentus. Ma. vența H. esculentus. Ka. bende esculent okra or edible hibiscus, H. esculentus Lin. Tu. bendè esculent okra, A. esculentus; kādu bendè H. abelmoschus. Te. benda A. esculentus. Pa. bendi H. esculentus. Kui bendi (should be bendi) id. Kuwi bendi id. /Mar. bhēļā, bhēdi H. esculentus. Turner, s.v. bhīſā or bhērā. (H. esculentus L. - A. esculentus W. & A. H. Abelmoschus L. is different.)

Ko. vet To. pet id., walking-stick. Ka. betta ratan, reed, cane. Tu. betta id., stick. Te. bettamu id. Kuwi (F) betti, (S) beti /Skt. vetra ratan (Calamus rotang) or other cane. Pkt. vetta id. H. bet id. Turner, s. v. bet.

Ta. vēlai, vēļai time, limit of time, seashore, sea, ocean, wave, sandy tract. Ma. vēla boundary, coast; point of time, hour; tide. Ko. vel-k, ve lt-k, ve lav-k, ve lavt-k, veletkat (such-and-such a) time. Ka. vēle time, season, opportunity, interval, leisure; the seashore, tide; vēle, vēlya time. Tu. Vēļè, vēlya time, period, opportunity. Te. vēla seashore, limit, boundary; vēļa time. Ga. (Oll.) vēla sun, daytime; (S) vēle Konda vēra id. Kui vēla id. Kuwi (F) verra, (S) vēda id. Kur. biſi id., time. Malt. béru ? Br. bēl half a day or night, one of the two daily meals. Skt. velā- boundary, coast, limit of time, period, time, hour, opportunity, tide.
